Also noted a second branch the finding does not: with paidUntil left NULL the effective-plan predicate at :180 passes forever, so the founding cohort silently keeps 1,000,000,000 caps instead of expiring. Both branches are wrong.

title: prod-bootstrap.sh treats tenant-schema migration failure as non-fatal — a green deploy can leave live libraries on an old schema
what: `pnpm tenant:migrate || echo "[bootstrap] tenant migrate skipped (non-fatal)"`. The migrate one-shot then exits 0, so compose's `condition: service_completed_successfully` is satisfied and api + worker start against tenant databases that did not receive the new migration. The same pattern is used for the first admin at line 54 (`pnpm admin:bootstrap || echo 'admin bootstrap failed (non-fatal)'`). Only the control-plane migration (line 35) and seed (line 41) are fatal.
impact: Ship a release that adds a tenant column; one library's DB is locked, out of disk, or its credentials rotated; that migration fails; the deploy reports success and the new API code queries a column that does not exist. That library gets 500s on every page while the dashboard is entirely green — nobody finds out until the librarian calls. For line 54: a completely green first deploy that nobody can log into, since the admin was never created (deploy-on-host.sh:75-79 warns only when ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL is empty, not when the bootstrap itself failed).
evidence: READ. scripts/prod-bootstrap.sh lines 49-57 quoted above; the header comment at lines 12-14 states the intent ('best-effort; new tenants self-migrate at signup, and a manual fan-out always exists'), but nothing in the deploy path performs or verifies that manual fan-out. docker-compose.prod.yml:207-209 shows api gated only on `migrate: condition: service_completed_successfully`, which a `|| echo` satisfies. deploy-on-host.sh's health loop asserts container health, never migration coverage.
fix: Make tenant:migrate fatal, or (better) have it exit non-zero and print the failing tenant slugs, and have the deploy either abort or automatically put the affected tenants into `read_only`/`out_of_order` system mode so they fail closed instead of serving broken pages. Make admin:bootstrap fatal on the first deploy (it is idempotent, so a failure always means something is wrong).
verification: Confirmed verbatim against the file. `cat -n scripts/prod-bootstrap.sh` shows lines 34-44 use `if ! pnpm db:migrate:deploy; then ... exit 1; fi` and the same for db:seed, while line 50 is `pnpm tenant:migrate || echo "[bootstrap] tenant migrate skipped (non-fatal)"` and line 54 is `pnpm admin:bootstrap || echo "[bootstrap] admin bootstrap failed (non-fatal)"`; `set -eu` at line 19 is neutralised by the `||`. The underlying script is NOT the sloppy part — scripts/tenant-migrate.ts:120-121 already does `log(... okCount ok, failCount failed)` and `if (failCount > 0) process.exit(2)`, i.e. it deliberately reports per-tenant failure with a distinct exit code that prod-bootstrap.sh then discards. Confirmed the gate: docker-compose.prod.yml:207-209 gates api on `migrate: condition: service_completed_successfully`, which a swallowed failure satisfies, and scripts/deploy-on-host.sh:181 checks only container health (`api=healthy web=healthy worker=healthy`) plus a static Caddy `respond "ok" 200` (infra/caddy/Caddyfile:136-140) — nothing in the gate asserts migration coverage. Searched for a compensating fan-out or drift check in deploy-on-host.sh and .github/workflows/deploy.yml and found none. Severity high upheld: the first deploy has no tenants so tenant:migrate is a no-op, but every release after that can green-light a fleet where one library's schema silently lags the code, and the admin:bootstrap half can produce a fully green FIRST deploy that nobody can log into.

title: The POSTGRES_PASSWORD 'CRITICAL guard' cannot detect a surviving cluster in the very scenario it was written for
what: `pg_data_initialized()` decides whether a Postgres cluster already exists by running `docker volume inspect --format '{{.Mountpoint}}' "${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-libriant}_pg_data"` and testing for PG_VERSION under that mountpoint. Two things break this in the documented topology. (1) The stated scenario is a 'boot-disk rebuild while the data volume survived' — on Hetzner a rebuild wipes /var/lib/docker, so the named volume's metadata is gone and `docker volume inspect` fails, the function returns 1, and the guard does not fire. (2) Deploys always chain docker-compose.volume.yml (deploy-on-host.sh:105), which redefines pg_data as a `local` driver with `o: bind, device: ${LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT}/postgres`; the local driver still reports `.Mountpoint` as /var/lib/docker/volumes/<name>/_data, not the bind target, so PG_VERSION is not found there either.
impact: The exact disaster the guard exists to prevent: a fresh boot disk with the data volume still attached, ensure-env.sh mints a brand-new POSTGRES_PASSWORD, writes it to .env.prod, and the Postgres container starts on the surviving PGDATA whose pg_authid still holds the OLD password. Every app connection fails authentication, the stack never comes up, and .env.prod has already been overwritten so the old password is only recoverable from a backup of a file the operator may not have. Total outage with a self-inflicted obstacle to recovery.
evidence: READ (docker is not installed in this audit environment, so the mountpoint behaviour could not be executed here). ensure-env.sh:67-73 quoted; docker-compose.volume.yml:22-28 shows the bind redefinition; deploy-on-host.sh:105 shows both files are always chained; docker-compose.volume.yml:5-6 states the premise 'a server "Rebuild" wipes the boot disk but KEEPS attached volumes'.
fix: Detect the cluster on the filesystem, not through Docker metadata: `[ -f "${LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT:-/mnt/libriant}/postgres/PG_VERSION" ]` (keeping the docker-volume check as a fallback for non-overlay hosts). Independently, store the generated .env.prod off-host (encrypted) as part of the deploy, so losing the boot disk never loses the password.
verification: Both failure modes confirmed by reading; could not execute (docker is not installed here — `command -v docker` returns nothing). Verified: scripts/ensure-env.sh:67-73 `pg_data_initialized()` requires `command -v docker` and then `docker volume inspect --format '{{.Mountpoint}}' "${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-libriant}_pg_data"`, testing `[ -f "${mp}/PG_VERSION" ]`; :80-85 is the guard that exits 3. Path (1) holds: infra/compose/docker-compose.volume.yml:5-6 states the premise 'a server "Rebuild" wipes the boot disk but KEEPS attached volumes' — that wipe takes /var/lib/docker with it, so the volume metadata the guard queries no longer exists and the function returns 1 (docker itself may not even be installed yet on the rebuilt disk, tripping the very first line). Path (2) holds: docker-compose.volume.yml:22-28 redefines pg_data as `driver: local` with `o: bind, device: ${LIBRIANT_DATA_ROOT}/postgres`, and deploy-on-host.sh:105 chains BOTH files unconditionally; a local-driver bind volume still reports .Mountpoint as /var/lib/docker/volumes/<name>/_data, which holds no PG_VERSION. I looked for a second, independent guard and found none: ensure-env.sh:96 `ensure_rand POSTGRES_PASSWORD 24` fires the moment the key is absent, and the surviving cluster's pg_authid is not consulted anywhere. deploy-on-host.sh:48/56 only assert the DIRECTORIES exist, which they will. High upheld — this is the failure mode of the documented DR path, and it destroys the recovery material (.env.prod) in the act of failing.

title: Re-importing a file after a failure silently duplicates every row without a natural key, including patrons' fines
what: The engine's idempotency contract only covers rows that HAVE a natural key it looks up. `commitFine` is a bare `fine.create` with no dedupe and `loanId` left NULL, so the `fines_one_outstanding_per_loan` partial unique index (which is `WHERE status='outstanding' AND "loanId" IS NOT NULL`) never applies. `commitBook` dedupes only on `isbn13`. `commitMember` dedupes only on memberNumber or email. `commitLoan` blocks only a duplicate ACTIVE loan. `commitReservation` relies on `reservations_one_active_per_book_member`, which is `WHERE status IN ('queued','ready')` only. Nothing records per-row progress, so any second pass over the file re-commits everything.
impact: A librarian whose 20,000-row import dies at row 12,000 has one obvious action: send the file again. Doing so doubles every already-committed fine, every ISBN-less book, every closed loan, every number-less member and every resolved hold. Patrons are billed twice with no marker distinguishing the duplicate. There is no de-duplication tool and no undo. Bulk import is the onboarding path for every new library.
evidence: RAN the real `ImportEngine` twice over the same one-row payload against the live tenant DB with duplicateMode='skip' (the safest setting): fine imported twice -> `FINES rows = 2 total cents = 1000` for a file that said 500c; ISBN-less book imported twice -> `ISBN-LESS BOOKS = 2`. Both passes returned outcome 'imported' with zero issues. READ: the `fines_one_outstanding_per_loan` index at packages/db-tenant/prisma/migrations/20260614000000_fine_one_outstanding_per_loan/migration.sql:36-38 is conditioned on `"loanId" IS NOT NULL`, and commitFine's create at import-engine.ts:683-694 never sets loanId.
verification: Reproduced the two sharpest sub-claims end-to-end (see evidence). Then attacked the framing: the original finding hangs the harm on `requireRunnable` (import.service.ts:332-345) letting a 'failed' batch be re-run. I checked whether that route is actually reachable and found the UI does NOT expose it — ImportWizard.tsx:61 lists 'failed' as TERMINAL and line 264 renders DonePanel, whose only action is `onAgain={reset}` (start over with a fresh upload). This does not kill the finding; it makes it worse. The realistic recovery is re-uploading the same file as a NEW batch, which duplicates identically, and there is no file-level dedupe (grep for checksum/sha256/hash in import.service.ts and import-staging.ts returns nothing), so an accidental double upload has the same effect. The crash-recovery sweep (import-queue.service.ts:103-158) sets wedged batches to 'failed' but does not auto re-run, so no unattended amplification. Severity upheld at high: silent financial duplication on the onboarding path, reachable by ordinary user action, with no undo.
fix: Persist per-row progress: record `(batchId, rowNumber) -> entityId` inside the same commit as the row and skip already-recorded rows on any re-run of that batch. Independently, give the fine/loan/reservation committers a natural key (e.g. a stable `importBatchId + rowNumber` marker column with a unique index) so a fresh re-upload of the same file cannot double-write. Until then, change the UI copy on a failed import from an implicit 'try again' to an explicit warning that re-importing duplicates rows already written.

title: No error boundary anywhere in the Next app — during an API failure every authenticated route, including /login, returns a bare English 500
where: apps/web/app/ (no error.tsx / global-error.tsx exists in the whole tree); apps/web/lib/session.ts:47
what: `find apps/web/app -name 'error.tsx' -o -name 'global-error.tsx' -o -name 'loading.tsx'` returns nothing — only `apps/web/app/not-found.tsx`. `currentSession()` (session.ts:40-49) swallows 401/403/404 but rethrows every other failure, including a raw fetch rejection (API unreachable). `LoginPage` (app/[locale]/login/page.tsx:23) calls it unconditionally whenever the request carries ANY cookie, because `requestCookieHeader()` returns the whole cookie header, not just the session cookie. With no error boundary, the throw escapes to Next's DefaultGlobalError.
impact: During any API outage the librarian cannot even reach the sign-in form. They get an unstyled, unbranded, untranslated English page reading 'This page couldn't load / A server error occurred. Reload to try again.' with no Libriant branding, no Greek, no support contact and no link back. There is no route in the app that degrades gracefully — the landing page and legal pages are the only survivors.
evidence: RAN: built the app (`NODE_ENV=production pnpm --filter @libriant/web build`, succeeded) then `next start` with `API_INTERNAL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:59999` (nothing listening). With `Cookie: __Host-libriant_session=bogus`: `/el/login -> 500`, `/el/signup -> 500`, `/admin/login -> 500`, `/el/t/demo -> 500`, `/el/t/demo/loans -> 500`. Server log: `⨯ [TypeError: fetch failed] { digest: '3227098399', [cause]: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:59999 }`. The 500 body is `<html id="__next_error__">` with an empty `<body>`. READ: apps/web/node_modules/next/dist/client/components/builtin/global-error.js — `children: "This page couldn’t load"`, `message = 'A server error occurred. Reload to try again.'`.
fix: Add `apps/web/app/[locale]/error.tsx` and `apps/web/app/global-error.tsx` that render a localized, branded outage screen (reuse the `illustrations/outage` asset and the `system.outOfOrder.*` catalogue keys) with a Retry button. Separately, make `LoginPage` tolerate a failed `currentSession()`: wrap it in try/catch and render the form when the session probe fails — a login form needs no session lookup to be useful.
verification: MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION, SEVERITY CUT FROM BLOCKER. I re-ran it against the existing production build (apps/web/.next) with `next start -p 3397` pointed at a stub API returning 503: `curl -H 'Cookie: __Host-libriant_session=bogus' /el/login` -> HTTP 500, body `<!DOCTYPE html><html id="__next_error__">` with an empty body element. Confirmed there is no error.tsx or global-error.tsx anywhere under apps/web/app (only not-found.tsx), and lib/session.ts:47 rethrows everything that is not 401/403/404. But the blocker rating does not survive two facts I checked. (1) `curl /el/login` with NO cookie header -> HTTP 200, the sign-in form renders fine; requestCookieHeader() returns undefined when the request carries no cookies at all, and I confirmed the web app sets no cookies of its own (`grep -rn "cookies().set|document.cookie" apps/web` -> nothing; no Set-Cookie on /el). So a first-time visitor is unaffected; only a browser that has already signed in is. (2) The harm is a degraded error page during a state in which the product is already unusable — signing in requires the API — with no data loss and no security consequence. High, not blocker: it must not displace attention from findings that lose circulation records.

title: Pulling the maintenance lever crashes every signed-in user: the takeover screen only renders for visitors with no cookies
what: The tenant layout's first act is `const [systemMode, impersonation] = await Promise.all([currentSystemMode(slug), currentImpersonation()])`, and only then checks `isTakeoverMode`. Two independent bugs make the takeover unreachable: (a) `currentImpersonation()` rethrows anything that is not a 401/403 (impersonation.ts:32), so on a 5xx or a network failure the `Promise.all` rejects before the takeover branch is evaluated; (b) `currentSystemMode()` returns the hard-coded `out_of_order` mode only for an `ApiError` — a raw fetch rejection (API process down, DNS gone, connection refused: the most common outage) falls to `return NORMAL` at system-mode.ts:53. So the branded maintenance/outage screen, its `illustrations/outage` asset and the `system.maintenance.*` / `system.outOfOrder.*` catalogue entries are dead code in exactly the situation they were written for.
impact: The takeover works ONLY for anonymous visitors. Every librarian who has ever signed in carries a cookie, so a planned maintenance window — and every unplanned outage — hands them a bare English Next.js crash page instead of the branded Greek maintenance screen. Executed: with cookie -> 500, without cookie -> 200 + Greek takeover. Operationally this means the maintenance feature has never worked for the population it exists for.
evidence: RAN both outage shapes against the production build. (1) API refused (ECONNREFUSED): `/el/t/demo -> 500`, and the RSC payload shows the layout error `6:E{"digest":"3227098399"}` — no takeover markup. (2) API answering 503 to everything (a Node stub returning `{statusCode:503,message:'upstream down'}`): `/el/t/demo -> 500`, log `⨯ Error: upstream down { status: 503, digest: '4172507616' }` — again no takeover, because `currentImpersonation()` rejected inside the same `Promise.all`.
fix: Make `currentImpersonation()` fail soft (return `null` on any error — an unreadable impersonation cookie is not an impersonation), and make `currentSystemMode()` return `out_of_order` for a non-`ApiError` rejection too, since 'cannot reach the control plane at all' is a stronger outage signal than a 5xx. Resolve the system mode before, not alongside, the impersonation probe.
verification: EXECUTED, and the finding is stronger than written. Read apps/web/lib/impersonation.ts:32 (rethrows anything not 401/403) and lib/system-mode.ts:53 (non-ApiError -> NORMAL): both mechanisms are exactly as described. Then re-ran the whole thing against the existing production build (apps/web/.next, BUILD_ID -eh04V7H-q4KJH3WJ5n38) with `next start -p 3397` pointed at a stub API that returns 200 + mode=maintenance on /system-mode/current and 503 on everything else — i.e. a DELIBERATE, PLANNED maintenance window, not an outage. Results: `curl -H 'Cookie: __Host-libriant_session=bogus' /el/t/demo` -> HTTP 500 with `<html id="__next_error__">`; the same URL with NO cookie -> HTTP 200 containing the Greek maintenance takeover ('συντήρηση'). Confirmed the cause is server-side: apps/api/src/system-mode/system-mode.middleware.ts ALWAYS_PASS covers /system-mode/*, /admin/*, /healthz, /readyz, /metrics, /webhooks/stripe and /apply — it does NOT cover /support/impersonation/me, so that endpoint 503s during maintenance, currentImpersonation() rethrows, and the Promise.all in layout.tsx:52 rejects before the takeover branch is reached. So the maintenance lever, when an operator pulls it on purpose, crashes every signed-in user instead of showing the screen built for it. Severity kept at high (no data loss, and the operator can undo it), but this is the worst finding in the dimension.

title: Every API error message is shown to Greek librarians in raw English; the translated errors.json catalogue is bypassed everywhere
where: apps/web/lib/api.ts:26-35 (ApiError.message = server text); 93 call sites render it, e.g. apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/loans/page.tsx:39, apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/loans/[id]/LoanActions.tsx:155
what: `ApiError` sets `message` to the API's `message` field verbatim, and the UI renders `err instanceof ApiError ? err.message : <fallback>` in 93 places. The API throws 336 exceptions (`grep -rn 'Exception(' apps/api/src | grep -v spec | wc -l` → 336), all with hardcoded English strings such as `'Member not found.'`, `'Due date must be after the checkout date — pick a later day.'`, `'Return time cannot be earlier than the checkout time.'` (apps/api/src/loans/loans.service.ts:153,161,371). Meanwhile `locales/el/errors.json` contains a complete, parameterised Greek error catalogue (13 keys, incl. `permission.denied`, `quotaExceeded.*`, `validation.*`) that is referenced from only 4 places in the entire web app — and in all 4 only as the fallback for a NON-ApiError.
impact: Every failure a Greek librarian hits in normal work — wrong due date, member already has too many loans, copy unavailable, no permission — appears as an English sentence inside an otherwise fully Greek UI. For a product sold to Greek municipal and school libraries this is the most visible quality defect in the app, and the localized copy to fix it already exists and is unused.
evidence: READ: `apps/web/lib/api.ts:30-31` `const friendly = Array.isArray(body.message) ? body.message.join(' ') : body.message; super(friendly ?? ...)`. RAN: `grep -rn 'err.message|instanceof ApiError ? err' apps/web | wc -l` → 93; `grep -rn 'Exception(' apps/api/src | grep -v spec | wc -l` → 336; `grep -rn "t('errors\." apps/web` → 4 hits, all fallbacks. READ locales/el/errors.json — 13 fully translated keys.
fix: Give every API exception a stable machine code in the body (`{ code: 'loans.dueBeforeCheckout', params: {...} }`) alongside the human message, and add a single `translateApiError(err, t)` helper in `lib/api.ts` that resolves `errors.<code>` from the catalogue and only falls back to `err.message` for unmapped codes. Route all 93 call sites through it.
verification: CONFIRMED. Read apps/web/lib/api.ts:26-34 — `super(friendly ?? ...)` does set ApiError.message to the server's English string. Re-ran the counts: `grep -rn 'instanceof ApiError ? err' apps/web` -> 90 (auditor said 93; same order of magnitude, claim stands), `grep -rn 'Exception(' apps/api/src | grep -v spec` -> 336 exactly. Spot-checked apps/api/src/loans/loans.service.ts:153 ('Due date must be after the checkout date — pick a later day.'), :159 ('Member not found.'), :371 ('Return time cannot be earlier than the checkout time.') — all hardcoded English. Read locales/el/errors.json: 13 fully translated keys, and `grep "t('errors."` returns only 4 sites, all as the non-ApiError fallback. Nothing refutes it.

title: When a circulation action fails server-side the error toast renders behind the modal's top layer — invisible and unclickable — and the modal never closes
what: In `LoanActions.call()` the success path and the offline path both call `setOpenModal(null)`, but the final `catch` branch (ApiError — 409 already returned, 403 role, 402 quota, 422 validation, renewal cap) only fires a `severity:'critical'` toast and leaves the modal open. `Modal` uses a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`, which places it in the browser's **top layer** — above every z-index — and makes the rest of the document inert. The toast stack lives outside the dialog at `z-index: 9000`, so it is painted under `.lbr-modal::backdrop` (`background: #0f172a99`) and is not hit-testable.
impact: The most common circulation failure produces no visible feedback at all: the modal just sits there. The librarian presses the button again. The idempotency key is (correctly) not rotated on error, so the retry replays, but the human has no idea what went wrong or whether the book was returned. Same defect applies to every other modal that toasts on error (BookDetail, MemberDetail, BarcodeScanner, data-model editors).
evidence: RAN: served a repro built from the real `packages/ui/src/styles.css` with a `showModal()`'d `.lbr-modal` and a `.lbr-toast.lbr-toast--critical` in `.lbr-toast-stack`, then measured in the browser: `document.elementFromPoint(toastCentre)` → `"lbr-btn lbr-btn--primary lbr-btn--md"` (the modal's button), and at the toast's close-button centre → also the modal's button. Screenshot shows the toast is not visible at all behind the backdrop. READ: LoanActions.tsx:152-157 — no `setOpenModal(null)` on the ApiError path.
fix: Two changes. (1) Close the modal (or render an inline `<Banner severity="critical">` inside the modal body) before toasting on the error path — inline is better here because the librarian is mid-task. (2) Render the toast stack into the top layer as well, e.g. via CSS `position: fixed; ` plus a `popover` / a per-dialog toast outlet, so a toast can never be occluded by an open dialog.
verification: CONFIRMED by reading the real code rather than a repro. apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/loans/[id]/LoanActions.tsx: the success path (line 111) and the offline path (line 145) both call setOpenModal(null); the final catch (lines 152-157) fires only a critical toast and never closes the modal — verified verbatim. packages/ui/src/Modal.tsx:44 calls dlg.showModal(), which puts the <dialog> in the browser TOP LAYER and makes the rest of the document inert; packages/ui/src/styles.css:589-598 puts .lbr-toast-stack at z-index 9000 in the normal layer, and :436 gives .lbr-modal::backdrop rgba(15,23,42,0.6) + blur. Top layer beats any z-index by specification, so the toast is both occluded and non-hit-testable. Also confirmed ToastProvider renders the stack as a sibling of {children} (Toast.tsx:72-74), i.e. outside every dialog. Also confirmed all three modals are mounted unconditionally at LoanActions.tsx:176-200, so this is the normal state of the page.

title: Offline circulation writes that can never succeed are deleted with a single 5-second toast and no persistent record
what: The replay loop deletes a queued action in three cases — expired (>18 h, OfflineQueueProvider.tsx:99-106), any 4xx (line 136), and after `MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS` 5xx retries — and in every case the ONLY notification is `toast.show({severity:'critical', title: ...})`. `ToastProvider` defaults `durationMs: 5000` and nothing passes an override, so the message auto-dismisses after five seconds. There is no failed-actions list, no badge, no server-side record, and `pendingCount` drops back to 0. The flush also runs on mount (line 178), so the whole batch can be dropped and announced before the librarian has looked at the screen.
impact: A librarian checks out ten books during a Friday-afternoon network cut, shuts the laptop, and opens it Monday. Every entry is now older than 18 h, so on mount all ten are deleted unreplayed with ten stacked toasts that vanish in five seconds. Ten books are physically out of the library and the system says they are on the shelf. The same silent loss happens for any single action the server rejects with a 4xx. The 18-hour expiry itself is a sound decision (it protects against double-applying past the server's idempotency window) — the defect is that its output is a disappearing toast instead of a durable, actionable list.
evidence: READ: OfflineQueueProvider.tsx:99-106 (`await removeQueued(action.id); ctx.current.toast.show({severity:'critical', title: t('loans.queue.expired', ...)})`) and :136-141 (same shape for `syncFailed`). READ: Toast.tsx:57 `const item: ToastItem = { id, durationMs: 5000, ...toast };` — OfflineQueueProvider passes no `durationMs`. `grep -rn 'loans.queue' apps/web` shows every queue outcome is toast-only; there is no queue/history screen anywhere in `app/[locale]/t/[slug]/`.
fix: Move dropped entries to a `failed` IndexedDB store instead of deleting them, and surface them in a persistent, dismissible panel in the tenant shell ("3 offline actions could not be saved — review") listing book, member, action and time, with a one-click 'redo this manually' deep link. Make the drop toasts sticky (`durationMs: null`) in the meantime.
verification: CONFIRMED. Read apps/web/components/OfflineQueueProvider.tsx:99-106 (expired -> removeQueued + one critical toast), :131-141 (4xx or attempts>=MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS -> removeQueued + one critical toast) and :172-179 (flush runs on mount, on 'online', and every 30s). Read apps/web/lib/offline-queue.ts:38 (MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS=6), :50 (MAX_QUEUE_AGE_MS = 18h), :53 isExpired. Read packages/ui/src/Toast.tsx:56 — `const item = { id, durationMs: 5000, ...toast }` and OfflineQueueProvider passes no durationMs, so 5s it is. Searched apps/web for any failed/dead-letter store or review screen: none — the only stores in lib/offline-queue.ts are the single pending queue. The Monday-morning scenario follows directly from the code.

title: Unauthenticated signup provisions a Postgres database per request with no admission control that an attacker cannot bypass
what: POST /auth/signup is unauthenticated and each success runs TenantProvisioningService: CREATE DATABASE plus a full Prisma migration fork, ~1.1s of server work and a permanent Postgres database. The only hard gate is the per-IP bucket `signup:ip:<ip>` (5/10min), which is keyed on the spoofable header from finding 02. The global bucket `signup:global` is deliberately advisory — alarmIfOverBudget() (auth.controller.ts:107-119) logs and returns, it never rejects. So after the IP key is defeated there is literally nothing left that refuses a signup. There is no CAPTCHA, no email-verification-before-provisioning, and no queue depth limit.
impact: One host can create tenant databases as fast as the box can fork migrations. Each one is a permanent Postgres database on the same cluster as every paying library, consuming connection slots, disk, backup time and the nightly DR window. This is the 'unauth signup DoS' critical the 2026-06 audit recorded; the remediation added a per-IP limiter, which the header spoof removes. The advisory-only global cap means the system has no backstop by design.
evidence: EXECUTED. 8 signups from a fixed `X-Real-IP: 7.7.7.7` -> 5x201 then 3x429 (the cap works). 8 signups with `X-Real-IP: 7.7.8.$i` -> 8x201, all provisioned. API log shows `Created tenant database tenant_cmt5mjvf2d566...` etc. for each. Tenants table went from 3 to 17 rows over the run; each request took ~1.15s of server time. READ: auth.controller.ts:107-119 `alarmIfOverBudget` only calls `this.logger.error(...)` and never throws.
fix: Fix the IP source per finding 02, then add an admission control that does not depend on the client's identity claim: provision the tenant database only after the owner clicks the email verification link (create the control-plane row immediately, defer CREATE DATABASE), and/or put a Turnstile/hCaptcha check in front of the form. Additionally cap the number of tenants in 'provisioning' state globally and reject (not just log) past that.
verification: REPRODUCED. With a fixed `X-Real-IP: 8.8.2.1`, 8 valid signups -> 201x5 then 429x3 (the per-IP cap holds). With `X-Real-IP: 8.8.1.$i`, 8 valid signups -> 201x8, no rejection. `select count(*) from pg_database where datname like 'tenant_%'` went 30 -> 43 across the run: 13 permanent Postgres databases created by one host in one loop. Read-verified the only other gate: auth.controller.ts:110-121 alarmIfOverBudget calls this.logger.error and returns — it never throws, and the comment (AUTH-05) says so deliberately. Also noted while probing: the throttle runs BEFORE validateDto (auth.controller.ts:135 vs :141), so even malformed bodies burn the bucket — which is correct behaviour, and confirms the bucket is the only admission control in the path. High is the right severity: it is a consequence of finding 02, not an independent defect, so it should not outrank it.

title: The DNS is not prepared for transactional email: SPF authorises only iCloud, there is no DMARC record, and the sending domain is the same one the campaign mails from
what: The product's default sender is `Libriant <no-reply@${PUBLIC_APEX_DOMAIN}>` (env.ts:387-390) i.e. no-reply@libriant.com, and site.config.json declares `notifyFrom: no-reply@libriant.com`. Live DNS today publishes `v=spf1 include:icloud.com ~all` and no `_dmarc` TXT record at all. Switching EMAIL_DRIVER to `resend` (the documented next step, docs/deploy-from-the-server.md:112) would send from an IP that SPF does not authorise, with no DKIM selector for the provider and no DMARC policy or reporting. This is not covered by 'no Resend key yet' — the key is one step; the DNS is a separate, unstarted one, and Resend also requires domain verification records before it will send at all.
impact: The first real emails Libriant sends — password resets, verification links, member overdue notices, and the 277-mailbox launch campaign — go out unauthenticated from a domain with no DMARC. Greek municipal and academic mail systems junk or reject that. The failure is invisible from the sending side: the outbox rows read `delivered`. A password-reset link that lands in a spam folder is indistinguishable, to the librarian, from the outage in finding 01.
evidence: EXECUTED `dig +short libriant.com TXT` → `"v=spf1 include:icloud.com ~all"` and `"apple-domain=KbpauxgxXHf5ijQq"`. EXECUTED `dig +short _dmarc.libriant.com TXT` → empty. EXECUTED `dig +short libriant.com MX` → `mx01/mx02.mail.icloud.com`. READ env.ts:387-390 for the default From.
fix: Before enabling any real driver: add the provider to SPF (`include:` alongside icloud.com), publish the provider's DKIM CNAMEs, and publish `_dmarc.libriant.com` starting at `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:...` so failures are visible, tightening to quarantine once the reports are clean. Verify with a seed send to a Gmail and an Outlook address and read the Authentication-Results header. Do this before the campaign, not after.
verification: RE-MEASURED TODAY, INDEPENDENTLY. `dig +short libriant.com TXT` → `"apple-domain=KbpauxgxXHf5ijQq"` and `"v=spf1 include:icloud.com ~all"`. `dig +short _dmarc.libriant.com TXT` → empty. READ env.ts:387-390 — default From is `Libriant <no-reply@${PUBLIC_APEX_DOMAIN}>`, and env.ts:383 shows the driver default outside development is `smtp`, so the moment a real driver is configured this address starts sending. `grep -rn -i 'spf|dkim|dmarc' docs/ apps/site/content/` (excluding docs/audit) returns NOTHING — the DNS work is genuinely undocumented and unstarted, which is the part 'no Resend key yet' does not cover. ONE CLAIM CORRECTED: the finding lumps the 277-mailbox launch campaign in with the unauthenticated mail. It should not — the campaign sends from the existing iCloud custom mailbox, which is exactly what the current SPF authorises and which already has DKIM. Only the *product's* transactional mail from no-reply@ is affected. SEVERITY HELD AT HIGH BECAUSE OF SEQUENCING: this is the blocker in finding 01's fix path. Switching EMAIL_DRIVER=resend without first adding the provider to SPF, publishing its DKIM CNAMEs and creating _dmarc gets password-reset links junked, and the failure is invisible from the sending side — the outbox row still reads delivered.

title: 'Daily backups with an off-server copy' is asserted in the offer terms and on the site, but nothing installs the cron, no offsite target exists, and no alert fires when either is missing
where: scripts/backup.sh:185-201; scripts/deploy-on-host.sh (no cron step); docs/deployment-hetzner.md:645; apps/site/content/programme-terms.en.md
what: Three separate gaps behind one published claim. (1) The nightly job is installed only by a hand-run `sudo tee /etc/cron.d/libriant-backup` in docs/deployment-hetzner.md:645. `scripts/deploy-on-host.sh` checks for docker, the data directories, the origin certificate and the admin email, but never checks that the backup cron exists — a completely green first deploy has zero backups and says nothing about it. (2) Offsite requires `RCLONE_REMOTE`, which `scripts/ensure-env.sh` does not default and .env.prod.example:101 ships empty; with it unset backup.sh:200 logs `WARN: RCLONE_REMOTE unset — NO OFF-SITE COPY` to a file. (3) `BACKUP_HEARTBEAT_URL` (backup.sh:206) — the only dead-man's switch — is not in .env.prod.example at all, so it will not be set by accident. Combined with finding 06 there is no alert destination, so all three warnings land in `/var/log/libriant/backup.log` and nowhere else.
impact: apps/site/content/programme-terms.en.md tells the first five libraries in writing: 'Your data is hosted in the European Union, with daily backups and an off-server copy.' /en/faq repeats 'with daily backups and a copy kept off the server.' On the box as the runbook actually leaves it, both halves of that sentence are false by default and stay false silently. The handbook is explicit that on a dedicated box 'backups are the only recovery option' (§8) — so the gap between the claim and the machine is the gap between a recoverable incident and a lost catalogue.
evidence: READ deploy-on-host.sh in full — preconditions at lines 46-77 cover docker/data dirs/origin cert/admin email; there is no reference to cron, backup.sh or BACKUP_ROOT anywhere in the script. READ deployment-hetzner.md:645 — the cron is a manual `sudo tee`. READ backup.sh:198-201 and :206-211. READ .env.prod.example — `RCLONE_REMOTE=` (line 101) blank; `grep -n HEARTBEAT .env.prod.example` returns nothing. READ ensure-env.sh — neither key appears in its ensure_default list.
fix: Add a precondition to deploy-on-host.sh that fails the deploy when /etc/cron.d/libriant-backup is absent or when the newest directory under $BACKUP_ROOT is older than 48h. Provision the Hetzner Storage Box and set RCLONE_REMOTE, or amend the site and the offer terms to drop 'off-server copy' until it exists. Add BACKUP_HEARTBEAT_URL to .env.prod.example and point it at a free healthchecks.io check — that one line is the difference between noticing a stopped backup tomorrow and noticing it in six months.
verification: ALL THREE SUB-CLAIMS RE-VERIFIED BY READING THE FILES. (1) `grep -n 'cron|backup|BACKUP' scripts/deploy-on-host.sh` returns only line 56 (a mkdir hint that happens to contain the word 'backups') and line 66 (a password-manager comment) — there is no check that /etc/cron.d/libriant-backup exists, no reference to backup.sh, no BACKUP_ROOT freshness test. READ docs/deployment-hetzner.md:644-649: the schedule is a hand-typed `sudo tee /etc/cron.d/libriant-backup`. (2) READ backup.sh:184-203 — the off-site branch is `if [ -n "$RCLONE_REMOTE" ]`, else `log "WARN: RCLONE_REMOTE unset — NO OFF-SITE COPY..."`, i.e. a line in a log file. `grep -n 'RCLONE|HEARTBEAT' scripts/ensure-env.sh .env.prod.example` → the only hit anywhere is `.env.prod.example:101:RCLONE_REMOTE=`, blank; ensure-env.sh mentions neither. (3) READ backup.sh:205-211 — BACKUP_HEARTBEAT_URL is the only dead-man's switch and, per the same grep, is absent from .env.prod.example entirely. THE PUBLISHED CLAIM IS ALSO REAL: `grep -rn -i 'off-server|off the server|daily backup' apps/site/content/` → programme-terms.en.md:66-67 'with **daily backups** and an off-server copy' and pages.en.json:1359 (/en/faq) 'with daily backups and a copy kept off the server'. So a written term of the founding offer is false by default on a green first deploy, and stays false silently because finding 06 means the WARN has no reader. This is the same silent-condition-with-no-observer shape as the DR restore that was broken for months. High stands.

title: Nothing tells anyone when it breaks: no Alertmanager, no uptime monitor, no on-call — the shipped alert rules fire into a dashboard that is not running
what: The monitoring stack is real (Prometheus 3.1.0, node-exporter, cAdvisor, Grafana) and the rules cover the right things, but the Alertmanager block in prometheus.yml:19-21 is commented out and no Alertmanager service exists in infra/monitoring/docker-compose.monitoring.yml. The handbook admits this at :389 — 'Prometheus does not deliver alerts by itself... the rules fire into a dashboard nobody is looking at. Until you configure that, treat the weekly sweep as your alerting system.' Separately, `scripts/deploy-on-host.sh` never starts the monitoring compose file, so on a fresh box even the dashboard is absent unless the operator runs it by hand. docs/cutover-three-hosts.md Step 7 says 'Repoint uptime monitors' — there is no evidence any uptime monitor exists; libriant.com/healthz has had no origin behind it since 2026-08-22 and nothing in the repo or docs names a monitoring provider or an on-call address.
impact: The detection time for any outage is 'until the sole operator next looks', which the handbook sets at weekly. That is the same class of failure as the DR restore that was broken for months: a silent condition with no observer. A library that opens on Monday to a 502 has no way to report it except an email address that, per finding 01, the operator may also not be receiving.
evidence: READ prometheus.yml:19-21 — the alertmanagers stanza is inside a comment block. EXECUTED `grep -rn alertmanager infra/monitoring/` — only those commented lines; no service, no config. READ server-handbook.md:389. READ deploy-on-host.sh — no reference to infra/monitoring. EXECUTED `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://libriant.com/` → timed out after 8s (no origin), so any monitor that did exist has been alerting or silent for a day and nothing in the repo records which.
fix: Before DNS is pointed at the box: (1) add Alertmanager to infra/monitoring/docker-compose.monitoring.yml with a route to a real destination the operator reads on a phone (email to a non-libriant.com address, or a push service — not an address that depends on the system being up); (2) add the two hardware alerts the handbook already names as missing (node_md_disks failed, NVMe percentage_used); (3) create external uptime checks on https://libriant.com/healthz and https://app.libriant.com/healthz with a third-party provider so an origin-down condition is detected from outside; (4) start the monitoring stack from deploy-on-host.sh, or check for it and refuse.
verification: RE-VERIFIED. READ infra/monitoring/prometheus.yml:17-21 — the entire `alerting:`/`alertmanagers:` stanza is inside a comment block. `grep -rn -i alertmanager infra/ scripts/ docs/` → only those commented lines, one comment in alerts.yml:5, and prose in server-handbook.md:389; there is no alertmanager service and no alertmanager config anywhere. READ server-handbook.md:389-393, which states it outright: without Alertmanager 'the rules fire into a dashboard nobody is looking at... treat the weekly sweep as your alerting system, and be honest with yourself that it is.' `grep -n monitoring scripts/deploy-on-host.sh` → no matches, so the monitoring compose file is never started by a deploy. RE-MEASURED `curl --max-time 15 https://libriant.com/` → 000 after 15s (no origin), so no external check is passing today either. NOTE FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: this overlaps docs/audit/pre-release-2026-08-23/findings/reliability.json:41 ('No alert is ever delivered to a human'). The mechanism is the same; the launch-readiness angle that is additive is the absence of any external uptime check and any on-call destination, which the reliability finding does not cover. Merge, do not double-count. High stands: detection time for any outage is 'until the operator next looks', which the handbook itself sets at weekly.

title: Public legal pages render the author's internal drafting note to visitors: the DPA opens with 'Replace every [PLACEHOLDER] and have it reviewed before you rely on it'
where: apps/web/lib/legal.ts:81; locales/en/legal/dpa.md:1-3 (and terms, privacy, cookies, acceptable-use, legal-notice, el/*)
what: That the legal documents are drafts is known. What is not is that the drafting instruction is inside the shipped markdown and is rendered verbatim to the public. `loadLegalDoc` does `marked.parse(raw)` on the whole file (legal.ts:81) with no front-matter or banner stripping, and the page injects the result (apps/web/app/[locale]/legal/[doc]/page.tsx:48). dpa.md lines 1-3 are a blockquote reading '> **Draft — pending review by qualified legal counsel.** This document is a tailored starting point, not legal advice. Replace every `[PLACEHOLDER]` and have it reviewed before you rely on it.' — so a visitor sees that above the app's own draft Banner. Unfilled bracket values render literally too: legal-notice.md shows '[e.g. Private Company (IKE) / S.A. (AE)]', terms.md shows '[exclusive/inclusive]' and '[via email at [CONTACT EMAIL]'. The route needs no auth (page.tsx:11 comment) and infra/caddy/Caddyfile redirects libriant.com/en/legal/* and /el/legal/* straight to it, so the marketing site actively sends visitors there.
impact: The audience for these pages is a municipal IT department, a bursar or a school's legal reviewer — the site says so explicitly and tells librarians to forward them. What they will read at the top of the Data Processing Agreement is an instruction to the author to fill in the blanks. Worse, apps/site/content/pages.en.json (/en/security) tells them 'The text is not published yet: it is with legal review and will be provided when it is ready' — while the same domain redirects them to the published draft. That contradiction, discovered by the reader, costs the deal.
evidence: READ legal.ts:78-83 — `const html = await marked.parse(raw, { async: true });` with `raw` the unmodified file. READ page.tsx:44-50 — `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: rendered.html }}`. EXECUTED `head -8 locales/en/legal/dpa.md` → the drafting blockquote is lines 1-3. EXECUTED `grep -o "\[[a-z][^]]*\]" locales/en/legal/*.md` → `[once per year]`, `[e.g. Private Company (IKE) / S.A. (AE)]`, `[exclusive/inclusive]`, `[via email at [CONTACT EMAIL]`. READ Caddyfile — `@moved path ... /el/legal/* /en/legal/*` → `redir ... https://app.libriant.com{uri} 302`.
fix: Strip the leading drafting blockquote in loadLegalDoc (drop a leading `> **Draft` block) so the internal note can never render, and fill or remove the bracketed values. Then decide one story and make both surfaces tell it: either publish the DPA and change /en/security's 'not published yet' sentence, or 404 the /legal/dpa route until counsel has signed off and drop the Caddy redirect for it.
verification: REPRODUCED EXACTLY. `head -6 locales/en/legal/dpa.md` → lines 1-3 are the blockquote '> **Draft — pending review by qualified legal counsel.** This document is a tailored starting point, not legal advice. Replace every `[PLACEHOLDER]` and have it reviewed before you rely on it.' READ apps/web/lib/legal.ts:81 — `const html = await marked.parse(raw, { async: true })` on the unmodified file, no front-matter or banner stripping. READ apps/web/app/[locale]/legal/[doc]/page.tsx:44-50 — `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: rendered.html }}`, and note :34-36 already renders the app's own `legal.draftNotice` Banner, so the internal author's note is both redundant and worse-worded than the one the product already shows. The route is public (page.tsx:11, no auth guard). UNFILLED BRACKETS CONFIRMED: `grep -o '\[[a-zA-Z][^]]*\]' locales/en/legal/*.md | sort -u` → [COMPANY LEGAL NAME], [COMPANY REGISTRATION NUMBER / GEMI], [CONTACT EMAIL], [DPO EMAIL], [SECURITY CONTACT EMAIL], [once per year], [PLACEHOLDER] — the literal token [PLACEHOLDER] appears once in each of six of the seven files. THE CONTRADICTION IS REAL AND IS THE WORST PART: infra/caddy/Caddyfile:285 redirects `/en/legal/*` and `/el/legal/*` from the marketing apex to app.libriant.com, while pages.en.json (/en/security) tells the same reader of the DPA 'The text is not published yet: it is with legal review and will be provided when it is ready.' Both sentences are served from libriant.com. High stands — this is public on day one, the audience is exactly the municipal/legal reviewer the site names, and the fix is a few lines.

title: The loans list — and therefore every dashboard load — sequentially scans the entire loans table
what: `loans.list` orders by `[{ loanedAt: 'desc' }, { id: 'desc' }]`. There is no index on `loanedAt` in packages/db-tenant/prisma/schema.prisma (loans has only memberId+status, copyId, dueAt, returnedAt, the customFields GIN and the partial unique on copyId). Postgres therefore reads the whole table and top-N sorts it for a 26-row page. The `overdue` filter (line 798-801) sets `status='active' AND dueAt < now()`; `loans_dueAt_idx` is useless for it because every historical loan has dueAt in the past, so that path also seq-scans.
impact: The tenant home page (apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/page.tsx:51-52) fires TWO of these on every render — `loans?status=active&limit=100` and `loans?overdue=1&limit=100` — plus the reservations list. At the Institutional size the loans heap is 256 MB while production Postgres runs the image default `shared_buffers = 128 MB` (infra/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml:320-325 sets only shared_preload_libraries and max_connections). Every dashboard view evicts the entire buffer cache of a Postgres instance shared by all tenants, so one large library degrades every other library on the box. This is the single most frequently hit page in the product.
evidence: RAN `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT id FROM loans WHERE 1=1 ORDER BY "loanedAt" DESC, id DESC LIMIT 26` on the 2M-row scale DB: `Parallel Seq Scan on loans (actual rows=666667 loops=3)`, `Buffers: shared hit=485 read=32360`, `Execution Time: 106.786 ms` — 32,845 8 KiB pages (256 MB) touched to return 26 rows, warm. Overdue variant: `Parallel Seq Scan ... Rows Removed by Filter: 661667`, 74.756 ms, 32,845 buffers. Prisma round trip measured at 224 ms wall for the full include (5 queries). `SHOW shared_buffers` = 128MB; `pg_relation_size('loans')` = 256 MB.
fix: Add `@@index([loanedAt(sort: Desc), id(sort: Desc)])` on Loan, and a partial index for the overdue path: `CREATE INDEX loans_active_due ON loans ("dueAt") WHERE "returnedAt" IS NULL` (or `WHERE status = 'active'`). Set `shared_buffers` explicitly on the postgres service (25% of PG_MEM_LIMIT, i.e. 512MB at the current 2g). Replace the dashboard's five list calls with a single cheap counts endpoint (see performance-11).
verification: RAN on libriant_scale. Unfiltered: `Parallel Seq Scan on loans (actual rows=666667 loops=3)`, `Buffers: shared hit=88 read=32757`, `Execution Time: 398.731 ms` cold. `status='active'` (the dashboard's first tile): same 32,845-buffer parallel seq scan, 363 ms. `status='active' AND "dueAt" < now()` (the overdue tile): 32,845 buffers, 58.8 ms warm. `SHOW shared_buffers` = 128MB; `pg_relation_size('loans')` = 256 MB — each of these queries touches twice the whole buffer pool. Confirmed by reading packages/db-tenant/prisma/schema.prisma:381-384 that Loan carries only memberId+status, copyId, dueAt, returnedAt — no loanedAt index, no partial index on the active/overdue predicate, and no index on `status` alone. Severity held at high: two of these fire on every render of the most-visited page in the product.

title: Member-number generation full-scans the members table on every create; the importer makes it quadratic
what: `nextSequenceForYear` runs `client.member.findMany({ where: { memberNumber: { startsWith: 'M-<year>-' } }, select: { memberNumber: true } })` — no `take`, no aggregate — and computes the max in JavaScript. It also omits `archivedAt: null`, so the partial unique index `members_member_number_unique_active` (which carries `WHERE "archivedAt" IS NULL`) cannot be used at all. The doc comment at line 32 asserts the opposite: "LIKE is fine here even on big tables because ... the column has a B-tree index via the partial unique index." The import engine calls it once per row (apps/api/src/import/engine/import-engine.ts:489) inside a 5-attempt loop, and each attempt is followed by `member.findFirst({ where: { memberNumber: candidate } })` — again without `archivedAt`, so again a seq scan.
impact: Adding one member to a 100,000-member library costs a full table scan and a 100,000-row transfer into Node. Importing a library's existing roster — the single most important onboarding action for an Institutional customer — is O(n^2): row k pulls k rows, so a 100k-row import moves ~5x10^9 rows. That import will not finish. The same scan also inflates the create transaction, which holds the max_members advisory lock.
evidence: RAN. `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE,BUFFERS) SELECT "memberNumber" FROM members WHERE "memberNumber" LIKE 'M-2026-%'` -> `Seq Scan on members (rows=100000)`, `Buffers: shared hit=2631`. Through Prisma: `nextSequenceForYear('M-2026-'): 100000 rows pulled into Node in 156ms, rss 89MB -> 279MB`. `EXPLAIN` of the importer's follow-up lookup `SELECT id FROM members WHERE "memberNumber"='M-2026-050000' LIMIT 1` -> `Seq Scan on members ... Rows Removed by Filter: 49999`, 1315 buffers; adding `AND "archivedAt" IS NULL` flips it to `Index Scan using members_member_number_unique_active`, 4 buffers, 0.567 ms.
fix: Replace the scan with `SELECT max(...)`: `client.$queryRaw` doing `SELECT max(substring("memberNumber" from '[0-9]+$')::int) FROM members WHERE "memberNumber" LIKE $1` — or better, drop the read-then-write entirely and use a Postgres sequence / a `member_number_counters(year, next)` row with `UPDATE ... RETURNING`. Add `archivedAt: null` to both lookups so the partial unique index is usable, or add a plain `@@index([memberNumber])`. In the importer, seed the counter once in `init()` and increment in memory, exactly as it already does for the quota counter.
verification: RAN `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE,BUFFERS) SELECT "memberNumber" FROM members WHERE "memberNumber" LIKE 'M-2026-%'` on libriant_scale: `Seq Scan on members (actual rows=100000)`, `Buffers: shared read=2631`, 30.6 ms — and `select count(*) ... like 'M-2026-%'` = 100000, i.e. the whole table is transferred into Node. READ member-numbers.ts:39-42 — the findMany has no `take`, no aggregate and no `archivedAt` filter, and `\di members*` confirms the only member-number index is `members_member_number_unique_active`, which is partial on `archivedAt IS NULL` and therefore unusable. The doc comment at line 32-33 asserting the column 'has a B-tree index via the partial unique index' is wrong. Importer path confirmed: import-engine.ts:445 `const memberNumber = number || (await this.generateMemberNumber())` and :486-497 loop nextSequenceForYear + an archivedAt-less findFirst, up to 5 attempts; apps/api/src/import/import.constants.ts:18 sets IMPORT_MAX_ROWS = 250_000, so a 100k-row roster import is permitted and is genuinely O(n^2). ONE NARROWING: generateMemberNumber only runs for rows whose CSV omits memberNumber — an import that carries the library's existing numbers is unaffected. Severity held at high: onboarding a roster is the first thing an Institutional customer does, and 'nothing happens for hours' is how it presents.

title: pinWorkerConnLimit() is a no-op, and the API's own ceiling is 250 connections against max_connections=200
what: `pinWorkerConnLimit` appends `connection_limit=1` to the tenant URL. That parameter is understood by Prisma's old Rust engine, not by `pg`. Under Prisma 7 driver adapters the pool size comes solely from `new PrismaPg({ connectionString, max })` (packages/db-tenant/src/client.ts:55), so the query string is silently ignored and the pool stays at `TENANT_DB_POOL_MAX` (default 5, packages/db-tenant/src/client.ts:21). Four cron jobs — fine-accrual, member-notifications, reservation-expiry, book-metadata-refresh — document this as their mitigation for 'PER-JOB-TENANTPRISMA-CONN-MULTIPLY'. Independently, the API's ceiling is `TENANT_CLIENT_CACHE_SIZE` (default 50, apps/api/src/config/env.ts:288) x 5 = 250 connections, against `max_connections=200` (infra/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml:325). pgbouncer does not help: it is configured with a single `DB_NAME: libriant_control` (line 349) and tenant URLs are derived from `PG_SUPERUSER_URL: ...@postgres:5432` (line 87, apps/api/src/provisioning/tenant-provisioning.service.ts:104), i.e. every tenant connection bypasses the pooler and hits Postgres directly.
impact: The connection budget the code believes it has does not exist. Past roughly 40 concurrently-active libraries the API alone can exhaust max_connections; Postgres then refuses new backends and every tenant sees 'too many clients already'. Because the pooler only fronts the control DB, there is no layer that can absorb the burst. This is invisible in a 5-tenant pilot and arrives all at once as the tenant count grows.
evidence: RAN. Built a client from the exact URL the jobs use (`postgresql://.../libriant_scale?connection_limit=1`), issued 20 concurrent queries, and counted `pg_stat_activity WHERE datname='libriant_scale'`: `open connections with connection_limit=1 in the URL: 5 (expected 1 if the pin worked)`. A control run without the parameter also gave 5, and idle sockets closed after ~10 s (pg's default idleTimeoutMillis), confirming `max` — not the URL — is what governs. Read: compose grep for the numbers above.
fix: Delete `pinWorkerConnLimit` and pass `makeTenantPrismaClient({ databaseUrl, maxPoolSize: 1 })` in the worker (the option already exists and is honoured), or set `TENANT_DB_POOL_MAX=1` in the worker service's environment. Independently, make the API's ceiling arithmetic explicit: either raise `max_connections`, drop `TENANT_CLIENT_CACHE_SIZE x TENANT_DB_POOL_MAX` below it, or route tenant DBs through pgbouncer as well (an `[databases] * = host=postgres` wildcard entry in a mounted pgbouncer.ini — all locking in the codebase is `pg_advisory_xact_lock`, so transaction pooling is safe; see performance-17).
verification: PROVED the no-op directly. Built three clients against libriant_scale and counted `pg_stat_activity` while 20 concurrent `SELECT 1 FROM pg_sleep(0.5)` were in flight: `URL connection_limit=1 -> 5 tenant connections`; `no param (default max) -> 5`; `maxPoolSize:1 option -> 1`. So the query-string parameter is ignored and only `PrismaPg({max})` (packages/db-tenant/src/client.ts:55-58) governs — pinWorkerConnLimit (fine-accrual.job.ts:36-40) is decorative, and the PER-JOB-TENANTPRISMA-CONN-MULTIPLY comment at lines 24-30 documents a mitigation that does not exist. STRENGTHENED: fine-accrual.job.ts:60-72 keeps ONE TenantPrismaService for the whole run and only destroys it in the `finally`, so a sweep holds min(activeTenants, TENANT_CLIENT_CACHE_SIZE=50) x 5 connections for its entire duration, and fine-accrual + member-notifications + book-metadata-refresh + reservation-pickup-expiry can overlap. Arithmetic re-read and confirmed: env.ts:288 cache 50, client.ts:21 pool 5, compose line 325 max_connections=200. pgbouncer cannot absorb it — compose:36 points CONTROL_DATABASE_URL at pgbouncer but :87 PG_SUPERUSER_URL at postgres:5432 directly, and tenant-provisioning.service.ts:104-109 `urlForDb()` derives every tenant URL from it by swapping only the path. High.

title: Erasure does not erase: the only member deletion is a soft archive, and the DPA states the opposite
what: `DELETE /members/:id` routes to `archive()`, whose entire mutation is `data: { archivedAt: new Date(), status: 'archived' }`. Every column survives: fullName, email, phone, dateOfBirth, addressLine1/2, city, postalCode, photoAssetRef, staffNotes, customFields. Loans, Reservations and Fines keep the memberId FK and their own `notes`. `grep -rn 'member\.delete|\.member\.deleteMany|erase|anonymi|pseudonymi' apps/api/src packages` finds no hard-delete and no anonymisation path in the product — the only `member.deleteMany` in the tree is packages/db-tenant/scripts/smoke-test.ts:86. On top of that the tenant audit_log permanently stores `{memberNumber, fullName, status, email, archivedAt}` in beforeJson/afterJson for every member.created / member.updated / member.archived (members.service.ts:71-87, 371-377, 461-465), with no retention job (see privacy-legal-05).
impact: A Greek public library that receives an Art. 17 request from a patron — or a parent acting for a child — cannot honour it through the product. There is no supported way to remove the person's name, date of birth or home address; the librarian's only options are to overwrite fields by hand (leaving the pre-edit values in the audit log's beforeJson anyway) or to ask Libriant for out-of-band SQL. The controller is in breach of Art. 12(3)/17 with no remedy, and the processor has contractually promised a capability it does not ship.
evidence: READ apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts:456-459 — `await tx.member.update({ where: { id }, data: { archivedAt: new Date(), status: 'archived' } })`. READ locales/en/legal/dpa.md:98 — 'The Service gives you tools to access, correct, export, and delete Controller Personal Data directly.' RAN `grep -rn "member\.delete\|\.member\.deleteMany\|erase\|anonymi\|pseudonymi\|gdpr" apps/api/src apps/web/app packages --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx"` → 7 hits, none an erasure implementation.
fix: Add a real `POST /members/:id/erase` that (a) nulls or tombstones every direct identifier on Member, (b) rewrites the memberId references on Loan/Reservation/Fine to an 'erased member' sentinel or strips their free-text notes, (c) redacts the identifier fields out of the tenant audit_log rows targeting that member, and (d) records only the fact and timestamp of erasure. Until it ships, change DPA §7 to say plainly that erasure requests must be sent to Libriant and are executed manually, and state the SLA.
verification: Re-read apps/api/src/members/members.service.ts:430-462: `archive()` is the whole of it and the only mutation is `tx.member.update({ where:{id}, data:{ archivedAt: new Date(), status:'archived' } })` at :456-459. members.controller.ts:133-141 routes `@Delete(':id')` to `svc.archive`. RAN `grep -rn "member\.delete|\.member\.deleteMany|erase|anonymi|pseudonymi|gdpr" apps/api/src apps/web/app packages --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` → exactly ONE hit, packages/db-tenant/scripts/smoke-test.ts:86. No erasure path exists. Confirmed the audit trail claim too: `memberSnapshot()` at members.service.ts:72-85 writes `{memberNumber, fullName, status, email, archivedAt}` into beforeJson/afterJson on create/update/archive. Re-read dpa.md:97-98 — 'The Service gives you tools to access, correct, export, and delete Controller Personal Data directly' — while the UI's delete button archives, so the DPA sentence is a misstatement. Downgraded from blocker to high. The mechanism is exactly as described, but the stated harm — 'the controller is in breach of Art. 12(3)/17 with no remedy' — overstates it. Art. 17 allows one month (extendable to three); an erasure request is answerable by out-of-band SQL from the processor within that window, and the librarian can overwrite the identifier fields in the UI in the meantime. Nothing here fails on launch day; it fails the first time a patron writes in, which is weeks away and manually survivable. It is not what wakes someone at 3am on Monday.

title: Member personal data is copied into the shared control plane and survives tenant deletion — contradicting the 'separate database per library' TOM in both the Privacy Policy and the DPA
what: The member-notifications job reads `member.fullName`, `member.email` and `copy.book.title` out of the tenant DB and enqueues them as `toEmail` + `bodyMarkdown` rows in the CONTROL-plane `email_outbox` table (one row per due-soon, overdue and hold-ready notice, forever, with no purge). support_action_log likewise stores pre/post state of touched member rows (schema.prisma:901-921) in the control plane. Both `email_outbox.tenantId` and `audit_log.tenantId` are declared `onDelete: SetNull`, so the admin hard-delete path (apps/api/src/admin/admin-tenants.controller.ts:157-217), which drops the tenant database and cascades the control rows, leaves these rows behind with `tenantId = NULL`.
impact: The single security measure both the Privacy Policy and the Art. 28 DPA lead with — 'isolation of each library's data in a separate database' — is untrue for the highest-sensitivity item in the system: an identified person's reading record. Borrowing history can reveal health, religion, politics and sexuality, and for school libraries the data subjects are children. After a library exercises its deletion right under DPA §8, its members' names, e-mail addresses and book titles remain in Libriant's own database, now orphaned: nothing links them to a tenant, so no future erasure or retention sweep can even find them. Under Art. 28(10) a processor that keeps and determines the fate of personal data outside the controller's instructions becomes a controller for that processing, with its own Art. 5/6/13 obligations that nothing here discharges.
evidence: RAN against the live control DB: inserted a tenant `gdprprobe` plus one `email_outbox` row (`toEmail=maria.papadopoulou@example.gr`, body 'Hi Maria Papadopoulou, "Το Κιβώτιο" was due on 2026-08-01…') and one `audit_log` row (beforeJson `{"fullName":"Maria Papadopoulou","email":"maria.papadopoulou@example.gr"}`), then `DELETE FROM tenants WHERE id='gdprprobe';`. Both rows survived with `tenantId` NULL — the SELECT after the delete returned the e-mail address, the member's name and the book title verbatim. RAN the FK query on information_schema: `email_outbox.tenantId → SET NULL`, `audit_log.tenantId → SET NULL`, every other tenant FK CASCADE.
fix: Either stop persisting rendered member-facing bodies (render at send time from ids and store only kind + recipient hash + status), or change `email_outbox.tenantId` and `audit_log.tenantId` to `onDelete: Cascade` and add a short-TTL purge of delivered bodies (privacy-legal-05). Correct Privacy §5 and DPA Annex II so the isolation claim names the exceptions.
verification: Independently reproduced end-to-end on the live control DB rather than trusting the auditor's run. RAN on libriant_control: `select conname, confdeltype from pg_constraint where conrelid in ('email_outbox'::regclass,'audit_log'::regclass)` → `email_outbox_tenantId_fkey | n` and `audit_log_tenantId_fkey | n` (confdeltype 'n' = SET NULL). Then inserted tenant 'vprobe', an email_outbox row (toEmail maria@example.gr, bodyMarkdown 'Hi Maria Papadopoulou, "To Kivotio" was due 2026-08-01') and an audit_log row (beforeJson {fullName, email}), ran `DELETE FROM tenants WHERE id='vprobe'` → DELETE 1, and both rows survived with tenantId NULL, values intact. Confirmed the producer: member-notifications.job.ts:213-236/246-272/288-313 selects `member.fullName`, `member.email` and the book title out of the tenant DB and passes them as `toEmail`/`bodyMarkdown` to the CONTROL-plane outbox. Confirmed the delete path at admin-tenants.controller.ts:186-217 does drop the tenant DB and delete the Tenant row. Re-read the two TOM claims: privacy.md:64-65 and dpa.md:85. Downgraded from blocker to high on impact, not mechanism. The 'separate database' TOM exists to stop library A reading library B's data, and that property is NOT broken: email_outbox and the control audit_log are reachable only by platform admins — no tenant-scoped route reads them (checked: the tenant export targets the tenant DB only). What is real is (a) a factually untrue sentence in a binding Art. 28 document and (b) PII that outlives a tenant hard-delete and is then unfindable by any future sweep. Both need fixing; neither is triggerable on launch day, since (b) requires an admin to hard-delete a tenant that does not yet exist.

title: No retention period is enforced anywhere in the system, while the Privacy Policy states retention periods as placeholders
what: SCHEDULED_JOBS contains nine jobs; not one deletes personal data on age. Nothing purges: control `email_outbox` (member names, e-mails, book titles, reset links), control `audit_log`, tenant `audit_log`, `support_action_log`, `support_redemption_attempts` (IP addresses), `applications` (site-form applicants), or `users.legalAcceptedIp`. `audit_log_retention_days` is declared as a plan feature and seeded per plan (7 / 90 / 365 / 1095 / 3650 / 1_000_000_000 days in packages/db-control/prisma/seed-data.ts), and the tenant schema comment at :562 says retention 'is enforced by a background job' — `grep -rn 'audit_log_retention_days|auditLogRetention|retention' apps/api/src packages` shows the key is never read by any code. Meanwhile Privacy §6 states the retention schedule as `[30]` days post-termination, `[14]`-day backups, `[up to 5–10]` years tax, and security logs `[a limited period, e.g. 90 days]`.
impact: Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation is not implemented at any layer, and Art. 13(2)(a) requires the retention period (or the criteria) to be stated — four placeholders are not a retention schedule. Concretely: a member archived in 2026 still has their name and e-mail in the tenant audit_log and in email_outbox in 2036; every IP address ever recorded at signup or in an audit event is kept indefinitely; and the plan feature the pricing page implicitly sells ('audit log retention: 90 days on Starter') is not delivered, which is also a consumer-facing misstatement. A library's own DPO cannot document a retention policy for a system that has none.
evidence: READ apps/api/src/jobs/registry.ts:23-83 — the nine registered jobs are support-session-expiry, reservation-pickup-expiry, stripe-webhook-retry, fine-accrual, export-file-cleanup, announcement-publish, book-metadata-refresh, member-notifications, storage-temp-cleanup. RAN `grep -rn "audit_log_retention_days|auditLogRetention|retention" apps/api/src packages --include="*.ts"` → hits only in packages/shared/src/features.ts:113-116 and packages/db-control/prisma/seed-data.ts (six seed values); no reader. RAN `grep -rn "email_outbox|emailOutbox" apps packages scripts infra | grep -i 'delete|purge|prune|clean'` → no matches.
fix: Add a `retention-sweep` job to SCHEDULED_JOBS that (a) deletes tenant audit_log rows older than the tenant's effective `audit_log_retention_days`, (b) nulls `bodyMarkdown`/`toEmail` on email_outbox rows older than N days (30 is ample for delivery troubleshooting) and deletes the rows after 90, (c) deletes support_redemption_attempts and control audit_log rows past a fixed window, (d) deletes `applications` at 12 months to match the published site notice. Then replace the four placeholders in Privacy §6 with the numbers the job actually enforces.
verification: Re-read apps/api/src/jobs/registry.ts:23-83 and counted the handlers: support-session-expiry, reservation-pickup-expiry, stripe-webhook-retry, fine-accrual, export-file-cleanup, announcement-publish, book-metadata-refresh, member-notifications, storage-temp-cleanup — nine, none of which deletes personal data on age (export-file-cleanup purges export FILES, not rows). RAN `grep -rn 'audit_log_retention_days|auditLogRetention|retention' apps/api/src packages --include='*.ts'` → the only hits are the declaration at packages/shared/src/features.ts:113-116 and six seeded values in packages/db-control/prisma/seed-data.ts (7/90/365/1095/3650/1e9). No reader anywhere, while packages/db-tenant/prisma/schema.prisma:562 asserts retention 'is enforced by a background job'. RAN `grep -rniE 'emailOutbox|email_outbox' apps/api/src packages | grep -iE 'delete|purge|prune|clean'` → no matches. Verified support_redemption_attempts stores `ipAddress` (schema.prisma:924-931) and that sweepExpiredSupportSessions does not prune it. Everything asserted checks out; a plan feature that is sold and never enforced is a second, independent defect. Severity unchanged.

title: Password-reset and e-mail-verification links are stored in cleartext forever in email_outbox, are not covered by the control-export redaction, and land in the Caddy access log that goes into the unencrypted backups
what: The reset body embeds the raw token — `${env.publicAppUrl}/${locale}/login/reset?token=${token}&slug=${slug}` — and the whole body is persisted as `email_outbox.bodyMarkdown`, a column nothing ever clears. The control-plane export redactor protects `users.passwordHash`, `users.inviteToken`, `support_keys.codeHash`, `tenant_db_credentials.*` and `stripe_webhook_events.payloadJson`, and its catch-all `if (/token|secret|passwordhash|password_hash/.test(c))` matches COLUMN NAMES only — `bodymarkdown` matches nothing, so an owner-admin export with scope `control` or `all` ships every reset link, verification link and support-key notification in plaintext to a 24-hour download file. The same URLs traverse Caddy, whose site-wide `log { format json }` block records the request URI including the query string; backup.sh step 3 tars that log into the daily backup, which is unencrypted and pushed off-site forever (privacy-legal-02).
impact: The Redis token TTL (60 minutes) is the only thing limiting exploitation, so a fresh backup, a fresh access log or a fresh control export is an account-takeover kit for any library owner whose reset is in flight. Independently of token validity, `email_outbox` is a permanent, unredacted archive of every transactional message Libriant has ever composed — member names, member e-mail addresses, borrowed book titles, applicant contact details — reachable through an ordinary admin export and through every backup. The `support_keys.codeHash` redaction is defeated in the same stroke, because the support-key notification body carries the code in the clear next to it.
evidence: READ apps/api/src/auth/password-reset.service.ts:79 (`const resetLink = ...?token=${token}...`) and :101 (`bodyMarkdown: body`). READ apps/api/src/export/export-processors.ts:59-72 — SENSITIVE_COLUMNS has no `email_outbox` entry; `isSensitive` tests `column`, not the value. READ infra/caddy/Caddyfile:25-31 — global `log { output file /var/log/caddy/access.log … format json }`, no URI/query filter. READ scripts/backup.sh:169 — `tar -C "$CADDY_LOG_DIR" -czf "$dest/caddy-logs.tar.gz" .`
fix: Stop persisting secret-bearing bodies: store a template id + variables and render at send time, or null `bodyMarkdown` immediately on `delivered`. Add `email_outbox: new Set(['bodymarkdown','toemail','subject'])` to SENSITIVE_COLUMNS regardless. Deliver reset/verification tokens as a POST-ed form value or a fragment (`#token=`) so they never enter a URL path, or add a Caddy log `filter` that scrubs `?token=`.
verification: Verified all four legs. (1) password-reset.service.ts:79 builds `${env.publicAppUrl}/${tenant.defaultLocale}/login/reset?token=${token}&slug=${tenant.slug}`, the token is interpolated into the body at :87 and the whole body is enqueued as `bodyMarkdown` at :101. (2) The redaction gap is real and worse than a missing table entry: export-processors.ts:59-67 SENSITIVE_COLUMNS has no email_outbox key, and `isSensitive` at :72-77 tests `column.toLowerCase()` against /token|secret|passwordhash|password_hash/ — a COLUMN-name test, so 'bodymarkdown' is never redacted. (3) Followed the export path further than the finding did: `readTables` at :364-380 enumerates `SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public'` — every table, email_outbox included — and only the `sql` format is blocked for the control DB (dumpSql :330-335), so csv/json/xlsx with scope control|all ship the bodies. (4) infra/caddy/Caddyfile:25-31 is a global `log { output file … format json }` with no URI filter, and backup.sh:169 tars that directory into the unencrypted daily. Severity unchanged.

title: A Redis outage takes down 100% of the API — including /healthz, /readyz and /metrics
what: `SystemModeMiddleware` is applied with `forRoutes('*')` (app.module.ts:118-127). Its `ALWAYS_PASS` list contains `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/metrics`, but the bypass branch still executes `req.systemMode = await this.modes.resolveGlobal()` (line 100) before calling `next()`. `resolveGlobal` → `readCache` (service line 231) → `this.redis.client.get(key)`. With `enableOfflineQueue: false` that rejects the moment Redis is unreachable, the rejection escapes the middleware, and the global filter turns it into a 500. There is no Redis-failure fallback anywhere in the mode resolver, and no in-process cache of the last known mode.
impact: Redis is a hard single point of failure for the entire product, and the failure is not graceful: every route returns HTTP 500 with a support code, the liveness probe reports 500, and the readiness probe reports 500 instead of its designed 503+diagnostics. Redis runs with `mem_limit: 512m` and no `maxmemory` (infra/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml:365-370), so a cgroup OOM-kill, an AOF rewrite stall, or a plain `docker restart redis` is a total outage of a library-management system in the middle of a circulation desk shift. Staff cannot check a book out; the readiness signal cannot tell an operator why.
evidence:
RAN. API booted against an isolated Redis, then `redis-cli -p 6391 shutdown nosave`:
```
healthz: 500
readyz : {"statusCode":500,...,"supportCode":"D72JZ1WC"} [500]
/auth/me   500
/t/reltwo/catalog/books?take=5   500
login      500
metrics    500
```
Server-side log line for D72JZ1WC: `"url":"/readyz","message":"Stream isn't writeable and enableOfflineQueue options is false","stack":"...at SystemModeService.readCache (...)"`. Recovery is automatic: 2 s after restarting Redis, healthz=200 and /auth/me=200.
fix: Two changes. (1) In the `ALWAYS_PASS` branch, do not resolve the mode at all — or wrap it: `req.systemMode = await this.modes.resolveGlobal().catch(() => NORMAL_MODE)`. (2) Make `SystemModeService.readCache/writeCache` fail-open: catch Redis errors, fall through to the control-plane query, and keep a short in-process memo (5–10 s) so a Redis outage degrades to a DB read rather than a 500. Add an integration test that kills Redis and asserts /healthz stays 200 and reads still serve.
verification: Mechanism REPRODUCED exactly, severity reduced. Booted the real API (apps/api/src/main.ts) against the audit stack, then `redis-cli -p 6390 shutdown nosave`: /healthz -> 500, /readyz -> 500 (generic supportCode envelope, NOT the designed 503+dependencies body), /metrics -> 500, /system-mode/current -> 500. Confirmed the cited line: app.module.ts:118-128 applies SystemModeMiddleware with forRoutes('*') and no exclusion, and the ALWAYS_PASS branch (middleware.ts:100) awaits resolveGlobal() before next(). BROADER THAN REPORTED: I also flushed Redis and stopped Postgres, and /healthz still returned 500 — because with a cold mode cache resolveGlobal falls through to `controlDb.systemModeEvent.findFirst`. Liveness therefore depends on BOTH dependencies, not just Redis. DOWNGRADED from blocker to high because the stated harm is bounded and self-correcting: I measured full recovery with no intervention and no restart within ~2 s of Redis returning (healthz=200, readyz=200); there is no data loss and no wedged process; and total unavailability while Redis is down is inherent to this architecture anyway — TenantResolverService (tenant-resolver.service.ts:95-107) and EffectivePlanService have no DB fallback either, so no request path would survive regardless. The genuinely fixable defect is the absence of fail-open on the probes and the mode resolver, which is a serious diagnosability failure, not a launch blocker.

title: Every session cookie is written verbatim into the API's INFO logs — harvested tokens authenticate
what: The pino redact list is `['req.headers.authorization', 'req.headers.cookie']` — request headers only. pino-http serialises the response with `pino-std-serializers.res`, which returns `{statusCode, headers: res.getHeaders()}`. `set-cookie` is therefore logged in full on every response that mints a session: `/auth/login`, `/auth/signup`, admin login, impersonation redemption, and every sliding-session refresh.
impact: The API's stdout — captured by Docker's json-file driver, 50 MB × 5 files per container (docker-compose.prod.yml:118-123) — is a rolling store of live, unexpired session JWTs (default remember-me TTL is 30 days). Anyone who can read container logs (host shell, a log shipper, a support bundle, an operator screenshot) can take over any account that logged in during the retention window, including tenant owners and platform admins. No credential, no MFA, no re-auth.
evidence:
RAN. Signed up a tenant against a live API, then grepped its own log file:
```
"set-cookie":"libriant_session=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJjbXQ1bWx4emowMDAwOXltdjJtM2pxdmMyIiwidGlkIjoi..."
```
Replaying that exact token straight from the log file:
```
curl -H "Cookie: libriant_session=$TOK" .../auth/me  ->  HTTP=200
{"user":{"id":"cmt5mlxzj00009ymv2m3jqvc2","email":"rel@example.com","role":"owner"},...}
```
Also confirmed the serializer independently: `pino-std-serializers.res(fakeRes)` → `{"statusCode":null,"headers":{"set-cookie":["lbr_session=..."],...}}`.
fix: Extend the redact paths to cover the response and every cookie name: `redact: { paths: ['req.headers.authorization','req.headers.cookie','res.headers["set-cookie"]'], censor: '[redacted]' }`. Belt and braces: supply a custom `serializers.res` that emits only `statusCode` and `content-length`. Rotate/purge existing logs on any host that has run this build.
verification: RE-EXECUTED. Two independent checks.
