Two book rows with the same ISBN-13 are therefore trivially reachable, after which `findBookByIsbn` returns an arbitrary one, so `duplicateMode:'update'` refreshes a coin-flip row and `resolveBook` attaches imported copies, loans and holds to a coin-flip row.
impact: The catalogue splits: the same title appears twice, its copies land under one entry and its holds under the other, and a re-import updates whichever row Postgres returns first. There is no merge tool, so the cleanup is manual re-pointing of copies.
evidence: RAN four `ImportEngine` instances committing the same isbn13 '9781234567897' concurrently against the live tenant DB -> `D) books with SAME isbn13 = 4`. Then RAN a direct `book.create` with the same ISBN (the shape BooksService.create writes) -> `E) after manual create, books with SAME isbn13 = 5`. READ: migration 20260526184041_init:305 `CREATE INDEX "books_isbn13_idx"` — non-unique; books.service.ts:206-234 writes `isbn13` inside the quota transaction with no preceding lookup.
verification: Mechanism reproduced exactly as claimed — both the concurrent-import route and the manual-create route. The DOWNGRADE is on severity, not substance. Three reasons the stated harm does not reach 'high': (a) the damage is catalogue quality, not data or money loss — nothing is destroyed and every duplicate is visible in search rather than 'invisible until a patron cannot find a book'; (b) it is repairable by hand today (re-point copies, archive the spare) whereas the high-rated findings have no user-side recovery; (c) it is the identical mechanism as data-integrity-06 (authors), which the same auditor rated medium — one of the two ratings has to move, and the author case is if anything the more reachable of the pair. Also worth noting for the fix: a hard unique index on isbn13 may be wrong for libraries that keep separate bibliographic records per edition, so the constraint decision is a product question, not a pure bug fix.
fix: Decide whether ISBN is a key. If yes: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX books_isbn13_unique_active ON books(isbn13) WHERE isbn13 IS NOT NULL AND "archivedAt" IS NULL;` (matching book_copies_barcode_unique_active at migration 20260526184041_init:470) and translate the resulting P2002 into the existing 'duplicate' path in both `BooksService.create` and `ImportEngine.commitBook`. If no: stop using isbn13 as the import's natural key and match on a composite the library controls.

title: Imported `ready` holds are permanently unfulfillable, never expire, and freeze renewals on that title
what: `commitReservation` writes a status='ready' hold with `readyAt` set but `fulfilledByCopyId` left null and no copy flipped to 'reserved'. Three downstream paths assume a ready hold owns a copy: `LoansService.checkout` refuses the pickup because `reservation.fulfilledByCopyId !== input.copyId` (loans.service.ts:269-273); `ReservationsService.resolveReservation` only frees a copy when `fulfilledByCopyId` is set; and the expiry sweep selects on `expiresAt: { lt: now }` (reservation-expiry.job.ts:92-95), which never matches when the import file carried no expiry date.
impact: The hold is immortal. It occupies the `reservations_one_active_per_book_member` slot so that member can never re-hold the book, and `LoansService.renew` (loans.service.ts:621-631) refuses every renewal of that title for every member while any queued/ready hold exists. Importing an existing library's hold list — the entire purpose of the reservation importer — wedges renewals on each affected title until a staff member finds and cancels each hold by hand. The patron is also emailed 'your hold is ready' for a book they cannot collect.
evidence:
RAN the real ImportEngine on one reservation row with status='ready' against the live tenant DB, with one 'available' copy of the book present:
  outcome imported []
  reservation: {"status":"ready","readyAt":"2026-08-23T10:14:01.034Z","expiresAt":null,"fulfilledByCopyId":null,"queuePosition":null}
  copy status: available
  expiry sweep would match (status=ready AND expiresAt < far-future): 0
verification: Reproduced verbatim — the orphan ready hold, the untouched copy, and the sweep matching zero rows even against a far-future cutoff. Checked each downstream claim in source rather than taking them on trust: loans.service.ts:269-273 does compare `fulfilledByCopyId !== input.copyId` and throws, so null blocks every pickup; loans.service.ts:621-631 does throw on any reservation in status queued|ready for the book, so renewals are genuinely frozen; reservation-expiry.job.ts:92-95 does filter on `expiresAt: { lt: now }`, and a null expiresAt is never `< now` in Postgres, so the sweep can never reach it. The one moderating fact — a file that DOES carry an expiry date escapes the immortality half — is already acknowledged in the finding. Severity upheld at medium: no data is lost and staff can cancel the hold, but the wedge is silent, self-inflicted by the documented migration path, and scales with the size of the imported hold list.
fix: In `commitReservation`, for status='ready' take the same `book:<bookId>` advisory lock the other allocation paths use, claim a copy with a CAS (`bookCopy.updateMany where status='available'`), set `fulfilledByCopyId`, and default `expiresAt` to `now + holdPickupHours` when the file has none. If no copy is free, downgrade the row to 'queued' with a warning issue rather than writing an orphan ready hold.

title: `authors.sortName` has no unique constraint, so the import's advertised author de-duplication is unenforced
what: The engine header (import-engine.ts:10-11) promises 'authors are find-or-created by normalized name so a catalogue import doesn't spawn duplicate author rows', implemented as `findFirst({ where: { sortName } })` then `create`. Nothing backs it: there is no unique index on `sortName` (only a btree and a trgm gin index), and `AuthorsService.create` at line 72 is a bare `client.author.create` with no lookup, so the UI happily creates the same author twice. Once two rows share a sortName, every later `findAuthorId` returns an arbitrary one.
impact: The author's bibliography splits across two rows permanently: browsing by author shows the name twice, each holding a subset of the books, with no merge tool. Because Greek names are accent-folded into `sortName`, near-identical spellings collapse to the same key, so the split is invisible in the UI until a patron searches.
evidence: RAN four concurrent ImportEngine instances each committing a book naming the same author -> `C) authors for one sortName = 4`, with the four rows sharing sortName 'nikos kazantzakis race' and four distinct ids. READ: authors.service.ts:72-82 creates unconditionally; migration 20260526184041_init:566 is `CREATE INDEX "authors_sortname_trgm" ... USING gin` and there is no unique index on authors anywhere in the migration set.
verification: Reproduced. Checked the two obvious refutations and neither holds: the engine's in-memory `authorCache` (import-engine.ts:110) does dedupe within a single run, and the import worker is `concurrency: 1` platform-wide (import-worker.ts:263) so two imports cannot race each other — but `AuthorsService.create` needs no concurrency at all to produce the duplicate, and that is the realistic route (a librarian adds the author manually, then imports a catalogue naming them). Severity upheld at medium: quality damage, visible, hand-repairable, no loss.
fix: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX authors_sortname_unique_active ON authors("sortName") WHERE "archivedAt" IS NULL;` and convert `findOrCreateAuthor` to an upsert on that key (catch P2002, re-read). Give `AuthorsService.create` the same lookup so the UI returns the existing author instead of a second row.

title: No timeout on any fetch — a hung API blocks every page for undici's 300 s default before failing
what: `const res = await fetch(url, init);` is issued with no `signal` / `AbortSignal.timeout`. Grepping the whole web app for `AbortSignal|AbortController|signal:` finds exactly one hit, in `app/api/readyz/route.ts` — the health check. Node 26's undici `fetch` has no default response timeout, so a server-side render blocks indefinitely; on the client every submit button stays in its `loading` state forever with no cancel.
impact: A wedged API (deadlocked Prisma pool, saturated Postgres, half-open TCP through Caddy) is strictly worse than a crashed one: the librarian gets a spinning tab that never resolves and never shows an error, so they reload, adding more hung server-side requests. There is no user-visible failure state and no server-side backpressure.
evidence: RAN: started a TCP listener on 127.0.0.1:59997 that accepts connections and never responds, pointed the production build at it, then `curl -m 45 http://127.0.0.1:3396/el/login` → `HTTP=000 time=45.006199` (curl's own cap; the request had not returned). Same code path serves every page.
fix: In `api()`, default `init.signal = AbortSignal.timeout(Number(process.env.API_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 10000))` (allow a per-request override for exports/imports), and map the resulting `TimeoutError` to a distinct, localized 'the server is not responding' state rather than letting it surface as a generic network error.
verification: PARTIALLY REFUTED. The defect is real: apps/web/lib/api.ts:103 is `const res = await fetch(url, init)` with no signal, and `grep -rn 'AbortSignal|AbortController|signal:' apps/web` returns exactly two lines, both in app/api/readyz/route.ts. But the finding's central claim — 'no default response timeout, blocks indefinitely, never shows an error' — is false, and the auditor's own curl test (capped at 45s by `-m 45`) could not have distinguished it. I measured it: a Node 26.7.0 fetch against a TCP listener that accepts and never responds threw after 301.0 s with UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT — undici's default headersTimeout is 300 s. So the real behaviour is a five-minute hang and then an error, which then hits frontend-01 and becomes a bare 500. Five minutes is still unacceptable for a page load and the fix is one line, but 'hangs forever with no error state at all' is not what happens, and a bounded-at-300s degradation under a rare half-open-upstream failure is medium, not high.

title: The moment BILLING_ENABLED is switched on, non-admin staff are locked into a dead-end screen with no sign-out and no navigation
what:
When `gate.billingEnabled && !gate.planSelected`, the layout `return`s a full-page takeover instead of the shell. For a librarian/volunteer it renders `

{libraryName}

{t('billing.choosePlanGate')}

` — a heading, a sentence, and nothing else: no sign-out, no link, no support contact. For an owner/admin it renders `ChoosePlanScreen`, which also contains no `LogoutButton` (grep for `LogoutButton|signOut|Link` in that 193-line file returns nothing). By contrast `DesktopGate.tsx:81`, the other full-page takeover, does include a `LogoutButton`.
impact: Flipping the subscription flag — the single most likely 'switch this on' event after launch — instantly strands every existing library. Staff cannot sign out to let an admin sign in on the same circulation-desk machine; they must clear cookies. An admin who does not want to pick a plan yet has no way out either. Combined with `price_seed_*` placeholder price IDs, the first plan click will also fail, on a screen with no escape.
evidence:
READ: layout.tsx:117-130 — the staff branch's JSX contains only `

` and `

`. `grep -n "LogoutButton|signOut|Link" apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/ChoosePlanScreen.tsx` → no matches; `wc -l` → 193. `grep -n LogoutButton apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/DesktopGate.tsx` → line 81 (the comparison case that does it right).
fix: Add the `LogoutButton` (and a 'contact support' link) to both the staff notice and `ChoosePlanScreen`, exactly as `DesktopGate` does. Consider making the gate a blocking banner over a read-only library rather than a full takeover, so an unpaid library can still see its data.
verification:
MECHANISM CONFIRMED, ONE EVIDENCE CLAIM WRONG, SEVERITY CUT. Confirmed apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/layout.tsx:117-130: the non-admin branch really does render only `

{libraryName}

` and `

{t('billing.choosePlanGate')}

` inside lbr-choose-shell, with no sign-out and no link; and DesktopGate.tsx:81 really does include . Also confirmed there is no GET logout route anywhere in apps/web/app — LogoutButton.tsx POSTs /auth/logout, so with no button there is genuinely no in-app way out, and /el/login would just redirect a signed-in user back to the gate. REFUTED DETAIL: the finding says grep for 'LogoutButton|signOut|Link' in ChoosePlanScreen.tsx 'returns nothing' — it has a support contact at line 154 (`href="mailto:hello@libriant.com"`), so the admin screen is not the total dead end described; only the staff notice is. Cut to medium: the whole thing is dormant behind BILLING_ENABLED=false, the escape hatch is clearing cookies rather than data loss, and the fix is importing one component.

title: The desktop shell's fallback page and custom menu are English-only, and the menu bar is half-localized by Electron and half not
what: A packaged build with no `LIBRIANT_APP_URL` and no saved config loads `https://app.libriant.com`. That host has no DNS record, so `did-fail-load` fires (main.ts:270) and the shell loads `static/fallback.html`. That page is entirely hardcoded English — `<html lang="en">`, 'Can't reach Libriant', 'The app couldn't load the library server…', 'Library server URL', 'Connect' / 'Retry' / 'Open in browser', 'Desktop bridge unavailable.', 'Something went wrong.' — and it displays the raw Chromium error string (`ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED`) to the user. Independently, the native menu built in main.ts:337-400 hardcodes English labels ('View', 'Connection', 'Reload from server', 'Safe mode (ignore saved server)', 'Open config folder…', 'Reset to default server', 'Check for updates…', 'Open logs…') while the adjacent `role: 'appMenu' | 'fileMenu' | 'editMenu' | 'windowMenu'` items are localized by Electron from the OS locale — so a Greek machine gets a menu bar that is half Greek, half English.
impact: The desktop app is downloaded from the tenant panel and is the paid-plan differentiator. Today every download launches straight into an English technical error demanding a URL the librarian does not know. Even after DNS is fixed, the shell's only offline/outage screen and its entire menu remain untranslated for a Greek-only customer base.
evidence: READ: config.ts:11 `export const DEFAULT_APP_URL = 'https://app.libriant.com';` (known state: this host has no DNS record). READ: main.ts:270-275 (`did-fail-load` → `loadFallback`) and static/fallback.html — every visible string is an English literal, including `errEl.textContent = (failedUrl ? failedUrl + ' — ' : '') + errText;`. READ: main.ts:352 `label: 'Connection'` and the surrounding template.
fix: Ship a bilingual fallback page (pick with `app.getLocale()`, or inline both and toggle with a `lang` query param the main process sets), translate the custom menu labels through the same locale, and either point `DEFAULT_APP_URL` at a host that resolves or bake the tenant's own URL into the installer served by `/t/:slug/desktop`.
verification: SOURCE CLAIMS CONFIRMED, FRAMING CUT BACK. Verified apps/desktop/src/config.ts:11 `export const DEFAULT_APP_URL = 'https://app.libriant.com';`, apps/desktop/static/fallback.html `<html lang="en">` with every visible string an English literal ('Can't reach Libriant', 'Library server URL', 'Connect', 'Open in browser'), and apps/desktop/src/main.ts:338-384 hardcoding 'View', 'Connection', 'Reload from server', 'Safe mode (ignore saved server)', 'Open config folder…', 'Reset to default server', 'Check for updates…', 'Open logs…' next to role-based items that Electron localizes from the OS. But the headline — 'the first screen on every fresh install is an error' — is a restatement of a KNOWN STATE the brief told us not to report as a discovery (app.libriant.com has no DNS record; nothing is deployed). Once DNS exists the fallback page is a rare screen. The durable, in-scope defect is that the desktop shell's only outage screen and its entire custom menu are English-only for a Greek-only customer base — the same class as frontend-13/15/18, hence medium.

title: No way to change language inside the app, and the tenant's own defaultLocale is never used — an en-US browser locks a Greek librarian into English permanently
where: apps/web/app/page.tsx:6-8 (only locale decision point); apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/SidebarNav.tsx (no locale control); apps/web/lib/api.ts:147 (`tenant.defaultLocale`, read but never used)
what: Locale is decided exactly once, at `/`, by `negotiateLocale(accept-language)`. `packages/i18n/src/locales.ts:25-35` returns `'en'` for any `Accept-Language` whose first supported tag is English. After that the locale is pinned in the URL prefix. The only locale switcher in the whole product is on the public landing page (`app/[locale]/page.tsx:77-84`, `.lbr-landing__locales`). There is none in the tenant shell, none on `/login`, none on `/signup`. `AuthMeResponse.tenant.defaultLocale` is typed in `lib/api.ts:147`, collected at signup (`SignupForm.tsx:112`) and displayed in the admin panel (`admin/tenants/[id]/page.tsx:270`) — but `grep -rn defaultLocale apps/web` shows it is never used to choose or redirect the locale.
impact: Greek libraries routinely run Windows/macOS in en-US. Those staff land on `/en/...`, get the whole application in English, and have no control anywhere in the UI to switch to Greek — they would have to hand-edit the URL. Anyone who bookmarks an `/en/` URL is stuck for good. The library-level language preference the product asks for at signup does nothing.
evidence: READ: app/page.tsx:6-8; packages/i18n/src/locales.ts:25-35 (`DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'el'` but any en-* Accept-Language short-circuits to 'en'). RAN: `grep -rn 'lbr-landing__locale' apps/web --include='*.tsx'` → only app/[locale]/page.tsx:77,82. RAN: `grep -rn defaultLocale apps/web` → 5 hits, none of which affect routing.
fix: Add a locale control to the tenant sidebar footer and to the auth cards (two links, same pattern as the landing page), persisting the choice in a cookie. On login, redirect to the tenant's `defaultLocale` when it differs from the URL prefix and the user has no explicit preference.
verification: CONFIRMED IN SUBSTANCE, SEVERITY CUT. Verified apps/web/app/page.tsx:6-8 (negotiateLocale on Accept-Language is the only decision point), packages/i18n/src/locales.ts:25-34 (any en-* tag short-circuits to 'en' before DEFAULT_LOCALE='el' is reached), and that the only locale switcher in apps/web is app/[locale]/page.tsx:77-84 on the public landing page. `grep -rn defaultLocale apps/web` returns 5 hits — SignupForm.tsx:112 (collected), api.ts:147 (typed), admin tenants pages (displayed) — none of which affects routing. What the finding omits, and what caps the severity: a user pinned to /en is not actually trapped. The landing page at /en carries the Ελληνικά switcher, so 'go to libriant.com, click Ελληνικά, then sign in' works, as does editing the URL prefix. That is a discoverability failure, not a lock-in. Medium.

title: The service worker serves stale API responses to online users — a newly created member is invisible on the first search after adding them
where: apps/web/public/sw.js:120 (`return cached || (await network) || Response.error();`), routed from sw.js:151-155
what: Every same-origin GET under `/lbr-api/` that is not in the `SENSITIVE` list goes through `staleWhileRevalidate`. That function returns the cached response **immediately whenever one exists** and discards the network result for the current caller, only writing it into the cache for next time. The caller has no way to observe the revalidation — there is no `clients.postMessage`, no `BroadcastChannel`, no re-render hook. So every client-side read is one round behind: `Combobox` member/book search (apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx:78), `AuthorPicker`, `DataTable.loadMore` (DataTable.tsx:110), help search, and the tenant export-status polling in `settings/export/ExportManager.tsx` all serve last-time's answer while online.
impact: At the circulation desk: add member 'Μαρία', go to checkout, type 'Μαρ' — if that exact query string was typed before she existed, the SW replays the old empty result and the picker says 'No matches'. The librarian concludes the member was not saved and creates a duplicate. The tenant export panel shows a permanently one-poll-stale job status, so a completed export appears to still be running. This is a correctness bug that only exists in production (the SW is registered only when `NODE_ENV === 'production'`, ServiceWorkerManager.tsx:17), so it will not be seen in dev or in any current test.
evidence: READ: sw.js:106-122 — `const cached = await cache.match(request); const network = fetch(request).then(...); return cached || (await network) || Response.error();`. READ: sw.js:151-155 routes all non-sensitive `/lbr-api/` GETs there. READ: ServiceWorkerManager.tsx:17 gates registration on production. (I attempted a live SW repro on a local HTTP server; service-worker registration is blocked in the audit browser, so this is a source-level determination — the control flow is unambiguous.)
fix: Use network-first (falling back to cache when offline) for `/lbr-api/` GETs instead of stale-while-revalidate. Correctness at a circulation desk matters more than the few hundred ms SWR saves, and the offline fallback is preserved either way. If SWR is kept for some endpoints, exclude all search/list endpoints and any polling endpoint.
verification: CONFIRMED at source. Read apps/web/public/sw.js:106-122: staleWhileRevalidate does `return cached || (await network) || Response.error()` and discards the network result for the current caller; :151-155 routes every non-SENSITIVE /lbr-api/ GET there. Checked the one plausible refutation — apps/web/lib/api.ts:96 sets `cache: 'no-store'` on every request — but RequestCache mode governs the HTTP cache only; it does not bypass the service worker's fetch handler, and Cache.match() does not consider it. Also confirmed the responses are same-origin (the /lbr-api rewrite), so `response.type === 'basic'` holds and they really are written to DATA_CACHE. ServiceWorkerManager.tsx:17 does gate registration on NODE_ENV==='production', so this is production-only as claimed.

title: Three simultaneously mounted Modals share id="lbr-modal-title", so the open dialog is announced with a different dialog's title
what: `Modal` hardcodes a single document-wide id for its title and points `aria-labelledby` at it. `LoanActions` renders `<ReturnModal>`, `<RenewModal>` and `<MarkLostModal>` unconditionally in the same fragment (only `open` differs), so three elements carry `id="lbr-modal-title"`. `aria-labelledby` resolves by `getElementById`, which returns the first match — the Return dialog's heading — regardless of which dialog is open. The same duplication occurs on the book detail page (BookDetail.tsx:371, 471), the member detail page, and the data-model settings page (AddFieldModal + EditFieldModal).
impact: A screen-reader user who opens 'Mark lost' hears the dialog announced as 'Return «Dune»'. On a destructive action (mark lost creates a replacement-cost charge) that is a genuine wrong-action risk, not just a nuisance. It is also invalid HTML on the highest-traffic page in the app.
evidence: RAN: served a repro reproducing LoanActions' exact structure (three `.lbr-modal` dialogs, the third `showModal()`'d) and evaluated in the browser: `document.querySelectorAll('#lbr-modal-title').length` → **3**, `document.getElementById('lbr-modal-title').textContent` → **"Επιστροφή «Dune»"** while the *Mark lost* dialog was the open one. The accessibility tree read back three separate dialogs each with its own heading, confirming all three are in the document.
fix: Generate the id per instance with `React.useId()` in `Modal` (and the same in `HelpDrawer`, which hardcodes `lbr-help-drawer-title`), and wire `aria-labelledby` to it.
verification: CONFIRMED without needing the auditor's repro. packages/ui/src/Modal.tsx:63 `aria-labelledby="lbr-modal-title"` and :74 `<h2 id="lbr-modal-title">` are hardcoded literals with no useId. apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/loans/[id]/LoanActions.tsx:176, :185, :194 mount ReturnModal, RenewModal and MarkLostModal unconditionally in one fragment, differing only by `open`. Three elements therefore carry the same id and getElementById resolves to the first (Return). Also confirmed the same hardcoded-id bug in packages/ui/src/HelpDrawer.tsx:52/:63 ('lbr-help-drawer-title').

title: Every dismiss/close control in the design system announces an English label to Greek screen-reader users, and one of them cannot be localized at all
where: packages/ui/src/Toast.tsx:96 (`aria-label="Dismiss"`, no prop); packages/ui/src/Modal.tsx:36 (`closeLabel = 'Close'`); packages/ui/src/HelpDrawer.tsx:34 (`'Close help'`) and :90 (`'Show help for this page'`); packages/ui/src/Banner.tsx:16 (`dismissLabel = 'Dismiss'`); apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx:56-57, :84; apps/web/components/DataTable.tsx:71-74, :123
what: The UI package exposes English defaults for accessible names and, in Toast's case, no override prop at all. Grepping the app shows that **no caller ever passes `closeLabel` (12 `<Modal>` call sites), `dismissLabel` (0 call sites), or `ariaLabel` on `HelpButton` (3 tenant call sites)**. Combobox and DataTable defaults *are* overridden by their tenant callers, but their hardcoded runtime error strings are not: Combobox.tsx:84 `setError(... : 'Could not search.')` and DataTable.tsx:123 `'Something went wrong. Try again.'` are the messages shown on a network failure and have no prop.
impact: A Greek librarian using a screen reader hears 'Dismiss', 'Close', 'Close help', 'Show help for this page' throughout a Greek interface. Sighted users hit the untranslated strings too: a dropped connection while searching the catalogue shows 'Could not search.' and a failed 'load more' shows 'Something went wrong. Try again.' — in English, in the middle of Greek pages.
evidence: RAN: `grep -rn 'closeLabel' apps/web` → only the two definitions in packages/ui, zero call sites. `grep -rn 'dismissLabel' apps/web` → zero. `grep -rn '<HelpButton' apps/web/app/[locale]/t` → 3 call sites (settings/page.tsx:35, settings/support-access/page.tsx:69, catalog/page.tsx:46), none passing `ariaLabel`. READ: Toast.tsx:96 has no prop to override. A repo-wide scan for hardcoded user-facing English in tenant-facing files returned 23 hits, listed above.
fix: Remove the English defaults and make the label props required (a TypeScript error is the right forcing function), add a `dismissLabel` prop to `ToastItem`, and thread the existing `common.actions.close` / `common.announcements.dismiss` keys through every call site. Move Combobox's and DataTable's runtime error strings to required props fed from the catalogue.
verification: CONFIRMED, every claim re-run. `grep -rn closeLabel apps/web packages` -> only the definitions in Modal.tsx:16/36 and HelpDrawer.tsx:12/34; zero call sites pass it. `grep -rn dismissLabel` -> only Banner.tsx:9/16; zero call sites. packages/ui/src/Toast.tsx:96 has `aria-label="Dismiss"` with no prop at all. HelpDrawer.tsx:107 `aria-label={ariaLabel ?? 'Show help for this page'}` and none of the 8 <HelpButton> call sites passes ariaLabel. The two sighted-user strings are exactly where claimed: apps/web/components/Combobox.tsx:84 `'Could not search.'` and apps/web/components/DataTable.tsx:123 `'Something went wrong. Try again.'`.

title: No skip link in the app and the main navigation landmark is named 'Sections' in English
where: apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/layout.tsx:209 (`<main className="lbr-shell__main">` with no preceding skip target); apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/SidebarNav.tsx:154 (`<Nav ariaLabel="Sections">`)
what:
There is no skip-to-content link anywhere in `apps/web` — a grep for `skip`, `#main`, `main-content` across `apps/web/app`, `apps/web/components` and `packages/ui/src` returns only unrelated import-wizard matches. Every tenant page places the brand link plus 8–11 navigation links plus the sign-out button ahead of `
` in tab order. Separately, the navigation landmark's accessible name is the literal string `"Sections"`, the only nav string in `SidebarNav` not routed through `t()`. Notably the marketing site does have a skip link (`apps/site/dist/index.html`: `Μετάβαση στο περιεχόμενο`) — the app that librarians use all day does not.
impact: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks, Level A. A keyboard-only or switch-access librarian must traverse the whole sidebar on every single page load before reaching the catalogue or checkout form. For a system used continuously through a working day this is the difference between usable and not. Greek screen-reader users additionally hear an English landmark name.
evidence: RAN: `grep -rni 'skip|#main|main-content' apps/web/app apps/web/components packages/ui/src` → no skip-link match. READ: SidebarNav.tsx:154 `<Nav ariaLabel="Sections">` versus every sibling label which uses `t('common.nav.*')`. READ: apps/site/dist/index.html line with `class="skip"` — the site does it correctly.
fix: Add a visually-hidden-until-focused `<a href="#lbr-main">` as the first child of the tenant and admin shells, give `<main>` `id="lbr-main" tabIndex={-1}`, and copy the `.skip` styles from the site. Replace `ariaLabel="Sections"` with a new `common.nav.sections` catalogue key.
verification:
CONFIRMED. `grep -rni skip apps/web/app apps/web/components packages/ui/src` returns only ImportWizard's duplicate-handling 'skip' enum and a code comment — no skip link, no #main target. apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/SidebarNav.tsx:154 is verbatim `
`, the only nav string not routed through t() (lines 82-93 all use t('common.nav.*')). Confirmed the contrast case: apps/site/src/shell.ts:734 emits `${esc(t.skip)}` — the marketing site has the skip link the app lacks. WCAG 2.4.1 (Level A) failure stands.

title: The entire email-verification flow is hardcoded English, and with EMAIL_DRIVER=console it is a permanent dead end
what: Neither file imports `createTranslator` or reads a catalogue. Every string is an English literal rendered inside a document whose `<html lang>` is the URL locale: the page title `"… · Verify email"`, the heading 'Verify your email', 'Verifying your email…', 'This link is missing its token.', 'The link may have expired or already been used. Sign in and resend it from the banner in your library.', 'Go to sign in', 'Go to your library', 'Your email is verified — thank you!'. The persistent shell banner is the same: 'Verify your email.', 'Some actions (like inviting staff) stay locked until you confirm it.', 'Resend link', 'Sent', 'Verification email sent — check your inbox.', 'Could not resend right now.' Additionally VerifyEmailClient.tsx:60 and :77 nest `<Button>` (a real `<button>`) inside `<Link>` (an `<a>`) — interactive content inside an anchor, which is invalid HTML and produces two focusable stops where the inner one does not navigate.
impact: This is the very first screen a new Greek library owner sees after signing up, and it is entirely in English. Worse, with `EMAIL_DRIVER=console` the verification mail only reaches the server log, so the banner never clears: the owner sees a permanent warning telling them staff invitations are locked, presses 'Resend link', is told in English that the mail was sent, and nothing ever arrives. There is no in-UI acknowledgement that email is not configured and no other route to verification.
evidence: READ: both files in full — no `t(` call and no `catalog` prop anywhere in either. READ: EmailVerifyBanner.tsx:27 `toast.show({ severity: 'success', title: 'Verification email sent — check your inbox.' })`. RAN: `grep -c '<Link\b[^>]*>\s*<Button' ` across apps/web → 2, both in VerifyEmailClient.tsx (lines 60, 77).
fix: Add an `auth.verifyEmail.*` namespace and thread `catalog`/`locale` into both components (the page is already under `[locale]`, so `loadCatalog(locale)` is one line). Replace `<Link><Button>` with `<Link className="lbr-btn lbr-btn--primary lbr-btn--lg">`. Until a mail provider is configured, have the banner detect `EMAIL_DRIVER=console` (surface it from `/auth/me`) and say so, rather than claiming a mail was sent.
verification: CONFIRMED with one correction to the finding's wording. apps/web/app/[locale]/verify-email/page.tsx DOES import createTranslator (line 3) and use it (line 10) — but only for the metadata title; the finding's 'neither file imports createTranslator' is wrong about page.tsx. Everything that matters holds: VerifyEmailClient.tsx and EmailVerifyBanner.tsx each contain exactly 2 occurrences of 't(' (both from unrelated identifiers, no translator), and the English literals are verbatim where cited — VerifyEmailClient.tsx:19 'This link is missing its token.', :62 'Go to sign in', :79 'Go to your library'; EmailVerifyBanner.tsx:23 'Verification email sent — check your inbox.', :42 'Sent'/'Resend link'. The invalid nesting is real: <Link> wrapping <Button> at VerifyEmailClient.tsx:60-62 and :77-79.

title: The public landing page's hero text fails WCAG AA contrast, as does the overdue-loan warning colour used as body text
where: packages/ui/src/styles.css:1165 (`.lbr-landing__eyebrow { opacity: .85 }`), the adjacent `.lbr-landing__hero-sub { opacity:.95 }` and `.lbr-landing__hero-note { opacity:.85 }`, over `.lbr-landing__hero`'s `linear-gradient(135deg, var(--color-primary), var(--color-accent))`; assets/theme/tokens.json:12 (`"warning": "#bf8700"`) as used at apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/loans/LoansTable.tsx:81, settings/activity/AuditLog.tsx:97, staff/StaffManager.tsx:209
what: Two independent contrast failures. (1) On the landing hero, white text is dimmed by `opacity` over a #1f6feb→#8957e5 gradient. Measured in the browser: eyebrow is 14px/600 at opacity 0.85, hero-note 14px/400 at 0.85, hero-sub 16px/400 at 0.95 — all 'normal text' under WCAG, requiring 4.5:1. (2) `--color-warning: #bf8700` is used directly as a text colour for the overdue-loan indicator and two `var(--fs-xs)` labels; against `--color-surface` (#ffffff) it measures 3.14:1.
impact: The hero is the first thing every prospective Greek library sees and the destination of the launch email campaign; the sub-headline that explains what the product does is the least legible element on it. The overdue marker is the single most operationally important colour cue in the loans table and is below AA for the librarians who most need to see it (older staff, bright reading rooms, cheap monitors).
evidence: RAN: rendered `/el` from the production build at 375×812 and read computed styles — `.lbr-landing__eyebrow` `rgb(255,255,255)` opacity 0.85 fontSize 14px weight 600; `.lbr-landing__hero-sub` opacity 0.95 16px/400; `.lbr-landing__hero-note` opacity 0.85 14px/400. RAN the WCAG formula on the composited colours at both gradient ends and the midpoint: eyebrow **3.78 / 3.99 / 3.80**, hero-note **3.78 / 3.99 / 3.80**, hero-sub **4.35 / 4.54 / 4.34** — all short of 4.5:1. RAN the same on `#bf8700` on `#ffffff` → **3.14**.
fix: Drop the `opacity` dimming on hero text (use a slightly translucent dark scrim behind the copy instead if the visual softening is wanted), or raise the values to 1.0. Add a separate `--color-warning-text` token (e.g. `#7c5e00`, already used as the banner's warning foreground and measuring >4.5:1 on white) and switch the three text usages to it, keeping `#bf8700` for borders and swatches.
verification: CONFIRMED — I recomputed the contrast independently and reproduced the auditor's numbers to two decimals. Read packages/ui/src/styles.css:1155-1197: .lbr-landing__hero is `linear-gradient(135deg, var(--color-primary), var(--color-accent))` with color #ffffff; .lbr-landing__eyebrow opacity .85 / --fs-sm / 600, .lbr-landing__hero-note opacity .85 / --fs-sm, .lbr-landing__hero-sub opacity .95 / clamp(1rem,2.4vw,1.25rem). Tokens: primary #1f6feb, accent #8957e5 (assets/theme/tokens.json:6,9). My own WCAG relative-luminance run on the composited colours: eyebrow/note 3.78 (primary end) / 3.99 (mid) / 3.80 (accent end); hero-sub 4.35 / 4.54 / 4.34 — all normal text, all short of 4.5:1 except the exact gradient midpoint for hero-sub. #bf8700 on #ffffff -> 3.14 exactly. Confirmed --color-warning is used as a text colour at LoansTable.tsx:81, AuditLog.tsx:97 and StaffManager.tsx:209.

title: The PWA manifest locks the app to portrait and ships SVG-only icons, so an iPad circulation desk cannot rotate and an iOS home-screen install gets no icon
where: apps/web/app/manifest.ts:21 (`orientation: 'portrait-primary'`), :24-42 (three SVG icon entries, one marked `purpose: 'maskable'`), :22 (`lang: 'en'`); apps/web/app/[locale]/layout.tsx:15 (`apple: '/_assets/brand/logo-square.svg'`)
what: `orientation: 'portrait-primary'` forces the installed PWA into portrait regardless of device rotation. Every declared icon is `image/svg+xml` with `sizes: 'any'`; there is no PNG anywhere in `apps/web/public` (`ls` shows only `offline.html` and `sw.js`). iOS Safari does not support SVG for `apple-touch-icon`, and the root layout points `icons.apple` at the same SVG. The manifest also declares `lang: 'en'` for a product whose default locale is `el`.
impact: WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.4 Orientation (Level AA) is a straight failure: a librarian who installs the PWA on a tablet mounted in landscape at the desk — the obvious deployment for a circulation station — cannot use it in that orientation. On iPhone/iPad the home-screen tile falls back to a screenshot of the page rather than the Libriant mark, which reads as broken to a customer being onboarded. The wrong manifest `lang` mislabels the installed app.
evidence: READ: apps/web/app/manifest.ts in full; apps/web/app/[locale]/layout.tsx:12-19. RAN: `ls -la apps/web/public` → only `offline.html`, `sw.js` (no raster icons at any size). Confirmed the emitted `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/_assets/brand/logo-square.svg">` in the live HTML from the running production build.
fix: Remove the `orientation` field (or set `'any'`). Add rasterised 192×192, 512×512 and 180×180 PNGs generated from `logo-square.svg` at build time, list the 192/512 pair in the manifest (keeping one as `purpose: 'maskable'`) and point `icons.apple` at the 180. Set `lang: 'el'`.
verification: CONFIRMED, with the headline scenario corrected. apps/web/app/manifest.ts is verbatim as described: orientation 'portrait-primary' (line 21), lang 'en' (line 23), three image/svg+xml icons with sizes:'any'; `ls apps/web/public` -> only offline.html and sw.js, no raster icon at any size; app/[locale]/layout.tsx:15 points icons.apple at the SVG. CORRECTION: iOS Safari ignores the manifest `orientation` member entirely, so the finding's specific 'an iPad circulation desk cannot rotate' example is wrong — the lock bites installed PWAs on Android tablets and phones, which is where it is honoured. The SC 1.3.4 (AA) failure and the missing apple-touch-icon raster (iOS does not accept SVG there) both stand. Kept at medium on the strength of the Android orientation lock, not the iPad claim.

title: Toasts auto-dismiss after 5 s with no way to pause or recover them, and the documented hover-to-pause behaviour does not exist
what: The component's own doc comment states 'Toasts auto-dismiss after `durationMs` (default 5s) unless the user hovers over the stack (paused).' No pause exists: `show()` sets `setTimeout(() => dismiss(id), item.durationMs)` with no hover handler, no `onMouseEnter`, no timer reset, and the returned handle is explicitly discarded (`void handle`). There is no toast history and no way to bring a dismissed message back.
impact: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (Level A): a time limit on reading content with no mechanism to turn it off, adjust it, or extend it. Concretely, toasts are the only channel for several irreversible outcomes — the offline queue's 'this action was lost' messages (finding-06), the fine-created and hold-promoted details attached to a successful return, and print failures. Anyone reading Greek at normal speed, using magnification, or simply looking away misses them permanently. The false doc comment means reviewers reasonably believed the mitigation was there.
evidence: READ: Toast.tsx:36-38 (the claim) against :44-66 (`show` / `dismiss`) and :72-104 (the rendered stack) — no mouse or focus handler anywhere in the file, and the `prefers-reduced-motion` claim in the same comment is honoured only in CSS (styles.css:662-666) which disables the animation, not the timer.
fix: Implement the documented pause: track hover and focus-within on `.lbr-toast-stack` and stop/restart the timers. Set `durationMs: null` (sticky) for `severity: 'critical'` by default. Correct or delete the doc comment either way.
verification: CONFIRMED. Read packages/ui/src/Toast.tsx in full: the doc comment at :36-38 promises 'unless the user hovers over the stack (paused)', and the implementation at :55-62 is `const handle = setTimeout(() => dismiss(id), item.durationMs); void handle;` with no onMouseEnter/onFocus anywhere in the file (the rendered stack at :72-104 has no mouse or focus handler at all). No toast history exists. This directly compounds frontend-06 — the offline queue's 'this action was lost' message is a 5-second toast with no way to pause or recover it.

title: Import staging writes 64 MB files to the shared storage volume with no quota, no batch cap and no cleanup sweeper
what: createBatch() stages the raw upload at STORAGE_ROOT/_imports/<batchId>.<ext>, up to IMPORT_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 64 MB per file. The file is deliberately excluded from the tenant's max_storage_mb quota (documented in the module header: 'Staged here rather than in tenant storage so the file does NOT count against the tenant's max_storage_mb quota'). Nothing else bounds it: there is no cap on how many batches a tenant may leave in 'uploaded' status, and the file is only removed by remove()/finish. Exports have a cleanup sweeper (apps/api/src/jobs/export-cleanup.job.ts); imports have none — grep across apps/api/src/jobs and apps/api/src/maintenance finds no reference to _imports, stagingPath or deleteStaged.
impact: Any tenant owner/admin (or one compromised admin account, or an honest librarian retrying a failing import twenty times) can fill the shared storage volume 64 MB at a time and never trigger a limit. That volume also holds every other tenant's covers and photos and is where export artifacts are written, so exhausting it breaks uploads, exports and the backup job for every library on the box at once. Abandoned batches accumulate indefinitely even without malice.
evidence: READ. import.constants.ts:7 `IMPORT_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024`. import-staging.ts:9-10 module header states the quota exclusion explicitly. import.service.ts createBatch() calls `stageFile(batch.id, ..., input.file.buffer)` with no preceding count/size check of existing batches. `grep -rn 'importBatch|_imports|stagingPath|deleteStaged|sweep' apps/api/src/jobs apps/api/src/maintenance` returns only export/announcement/fine/reservation sweepers — no import sweeper exists.
fix: Two lines of defence: (a) in createBatch, refuse when the tenant already has N batches in status 'uploaded'/'mapped' (N=3 is generous) or when the sum of their sizeBytes exceeds a per-tenant staging budget; (b) add a sweeper alongside sweepExpiredExports that deletes staged files and rows for batches left un-run for more than ~24h.
verification: Read-verified in full and one implicit claim corrected. import.constants.ts:7 is 64 MB and import.controller.ts:70 applies it as the only multer limit. import.service.ts createBatch (lines 45-105) performs no count or size check against the tenant's existing batches before calling stageFile at line 101 — I read the whole function. The quota exclusion is explicit at import-staging.ts:6-8. CORRECTION: a sweeper file DOES exist — apps/api/src/jobs/storage-temp-cleanup.job.ts — so 'imports have none' needed checking rather than asserting. I read it: it walks active tenants and calls driver.sweepStaleTemps(maxAgeMs) to delete `<target>.tmp-<hex>` partials inside TENANT storage. It never touches STORAGE_ROOT/_imports. The other candidate, import-queue.service.ts sweepStuckBatches (lines 110-160), reclaims stuck batches to 'failed' and its comment states 'Keep the staged file' deliberately so a re-run works — i.e. the one job that visits abandoned batches is explicitly designed NOT to delete their files. So nothing ever removes a staged file for a batch left in 'uploaded'. Also confirmed no disk-space guard anywhere in apps/api/src (no statfs/df/free-bytes check). Medium upheld: it needs an authenticated owner/admin, so it is not an anonymous lever, but the blast radius is the shared volume holding every tenant's covers plus export artifacts.

title: The launch offer is not mechanically deliverable: putting a tenant on Municipal forces billingMode=stripe, and set-paid-until then refuses — the documented founding-library procedure returns 400
what: docs/billing-go-live.md:115 states the go-live precondition: "Founding-offer libraries must be on `billingMode = 'manual'` with `paidUntil` twelve months out before this flips, or they get charged for what they were promised free." That state cannot be reached. `applyAdminPlanChange` writes `billingMode: plan.billingMode` (billing.service.ts:414) — denormalised from the plan — and every sellable plan is seeded `stripe`; only `on-prem-enterprise` is `manual`. `applyManualPayment` then hard-refuses: `if (sub.billingMode !== 'manual') throw new BadRequestException('Manual paid-until only applies to manually-billed plans...')` (billing.service.ts:452-456). There is no admin endpoint that sets `subscription.billingMode` independently of the plan. Consequently a founding library placed on Municipal sits at `billingMode=stripe, status=active, stripeSubscriptionId=null, paidUntil=null`, and EffectivePlanService's join (effective-plan.service.ts:180) only expires `manual` subscriptions — so the twelve months have no end date and nothing in the system will ever end them.
impact: Two failure modes, both commercial. Before billing is switched on the five founding libraries can only be granted Municipal by leaving them in a state the go-live runbook explicitly forbids; when BILLING_ENABLED flips they either get gated wrongly or stay free forever with no expiry and no dunning. The offer terms promise 'the account simply stops being active' at month thirteen (apps/site/content/programme-terms.en.md) — no code path produces that outcome.
evidence: EXECUTED against the live audit environment via the admin API: `### SET-PLAN municipal 201 {"tenantId":"cmt5n37xm...","billingMode":"stripe","status":"active","plan":{"slug":"municipal"},"paidUntil":null,...}` then `### SET-PAID-UNTIL 400 {"message":"Manual paid-until only applies to manually-billed plans. Use Stripe for stripe-billed tenants.","statusCode":400}`. EXECUTED `psql -c 'select slug, "billingMode" from plans'` → starter/community/municipal/central/institutional all `stripe`; only `on-prem-enterprise` is `manual`.
fix: Add an owner-only admin action that sets `subscription.billingMode='manual'` together with `paidUntil` (one endpoint, audited), or seed a dedicated `founding-municipal` plan with `billingMode='manual'` and the Municipal feature values and place the five libraries on it. Then walk one tenant through the full path — set plan, set paidUntil 12 months out, flip BILLING_ENABLED=true, confirm features stay on and confirm they drop the day after paidUntil — before any library is told they have a place.
verification: MECHANISM REPRODUCED, IMPACT DOES NOT FOLLOW AT BLOCKER LEVEL. My own probe against the live audit environment: `SET-PLAN 201 {..."billingMode":"stripe"..."plan":{"slug":"municipal"}...}` then `SET-PAID-UNTIL 400 {"message":"Manual paid-until only applies to manually-billed plans..."}`, and the row afterwards reads `{billingMode: stripe, status: active, paidUntil: null, planSelectedAt: null, stripeSubscriptionId: null}`. READ billing.service.ts:414 (`billingMode: plan.billingMode`) and :452-456 (the refusal). `psql -c 'select slug, "billingMode" from plans'` → only on-prem-enterprise is manual. `grep -rn billingMode apps/api/src/billing apps/api/src/plans` finds no writer that sets it independently of the plan. All confirmed. BUT HALF THE STATED IMPACT IS FALSE. The finding says the founding libraries 'either get gated wrongly or stay free forever'. Gated wrongly does not happen: effective-plan.service.ts:168-180 joins on `s.status IN ('active','trialing')` and the manual-expiry clause at :180 is skipped for billingMode<>'manual', so a Municipal/stripe/active tenant resolves the full Municipal feature set with or without BILLING_ENABLED. Nobody is charged either — there is no stripeSubscriptionId. The only real consequence is the one the finding lands second: the twelve months have no end date. AND A WORKAROUND THE FINDING DID NOT CONSIDER EXISTS TODAY: admin-overrides.controller.ts (PUT /admin/tenants/:id/overrides) grants per-feature values with an `expiresAt`, honoured by effective-plan.service.ts:186 (`tpo."expiresAt" IS NULL OR tpo."expiresAt" > NOW()`) and cache-clamped at :215-229. Clunky, but it delivers a dated twelve-month grant without touching billingMode. TIMING: the harm is entirely at month thirteen, i.e. >12 months out and also gated behind company registration. The fix is a one-row seed change. Real defect, correctly found, wrong severity — at blocker it displaces attention from things that break on Monday.

title: The commercial funnel has no notification and no admin screen: an application lands in Postgres and nobody is told, while the site promises an answer within two working days
what: `ApplicationsService.notify` enqueues an `application_submitted` email to `applyNotifyTo` (info@libriant.com). That enqueue goes through the same EmailService as everything else, so under EMAIL_DRIVER=console it is logged-and-dropped (see finding 01). There is no fallback channel — no webhook, no Slack, no admin badge. On the read side the admin panel has no Applications page: the directory listing of apps/web/app/[locale]/admin/(authed)/ contains announcements, export, fleet, library-requests, maintenance, mfa, plans, subscriptions, support, system-mode, tenants — and nothing for applications; AdminSidebar.tsx:32-42 lists the same eleven items. The only read path is a bare CSV route, `GET /admin/applications.csv` (apps/api/src/applications/applications.controller.ts:113), which is not linked from anywhere in the UI.
impact: The launch campaign drives 277 mailboxes to a form whose submissions are invisible. apps/site/content/pages.en.json (/en/contact, /en/faq) promises 'We answer every application within two working days, yes or no' and 'No question is left unanswered on purpose'. The first five founding places are awarded 'in order of application' — an order nobody can observe. Leads are not lost (the row commits) but they are silently unread until someone thinks to type a URL that appears in no menu.
evidence: READ applications.service.ts:169-186 — the notification is `this.email.enqueue({ kind: 'application_submitted', toEmail: this.notifyTo, ... })`, the only delivery mechanism. EXECUTED `ls 'apps/web/app/[locale]/admin/(authed)/'` → no `applications` directory. READ AdminSidebar.tsx:32-42 — eleven nav entries, none for applications. READ pages.en.json /en/contact: 'We answer every message within two working days.'
fix: Before the campaign sends: add an Applications page to the admin panel (list + status + the CSV as a download button), and give the notification a delivery path that does not depend on the mail driver — at minimum a startup-time refusal to run with `EMAIL_DRIVER=console` while `spotsRemaining > 0`, at best a real mailbox via finding 04.
verification: MECHANISM CONFIRMED, NOT A BLOCKER. `ls 'apps/web/app/[locale]/admin/(authed)/'` → AdminSidebar.tsx, announcements, export, fleet, layout.tsx, library-requests, maintenance, mfa, page.tsx, plans, subscriptions, support, system-mode, tenants — no applications directory. READ AdminSidebar.tsx:31-42, eleven links, none for applications. `grep -rn applications apps/web/app apps/web/lib apps/web/components` returns NOTHING, so /admin/applications.csv is genuinely unlinked. READ applications.service.ts:169-186 — the sole notification is `this.email.enqueue({kind:'application_submitted', ...})`, which under console is dropped per finding 01. All true. BUT THE IMPACT IS NOT BLOCKER-SHAPED. The finding itself concedes leads are not lost — applications.controller.ts:88-97 commits the row before notifying, and even the save-failure branch (:90) attempts a notify and tells the applicant another contact route. The CSV export exists and works behind an admin session (applications.controller.ts:113 + AdminAuthGuard/AdminRolesGuard). The mitigation is a bookmark. No user is harmed, no data is destroyed, nothing is silent to the one person who wrote the form and is running the campaign. Per the project's own launch plan the campaign does not send in August, so the funnel is not even live on Monday. Medium: a real day-one operational hole in the commercial funnel, fixable with an admin page or a single bookmarked URL.

title: admin.libriant.com is already live in DNS pointing at a released IP, and neither cutover document knows the record exists
what: Both documents inventory DNS as 'libriant.com resolves to Cloudflare with no origin, app.libriant.com has no A record' and instruct the operator to add only the `app` record at Step 2. That inventory is incomplete: `admin.libriant.com` already resolves, proxied through Cloudflare, and hangs — its origin is the decommissioned 178.104.32.176, an address Hetzner has taken back and will reassign. Step 2's guidance ('No new certificate is needed... verify before proceeding') is written for a record being created, not for one that already exists and points somewhere wrong. Nothing in the cutover sequence repoints or deletes it.
impact: Two things. Operationally, an operator following cutover-three-hosts.md end to end deploys the box, adds `app`, verifies TLS, and never touches `admin` — which then continues to proxy to whoever now holds 178.104.32.176. If Cloudflare's SSL/TLS mode is anything other than Full (strict), admin.libriant.com — the host that serves the admin login — proxies to a stranger's server on a hostname covered by the origin certificate and by HSTS includeSubDomains. Commercially, a prospect who tries the admin host today gets an 8-second hang rather than a page.
evidence: EXECUTED `dig +short admin.libriant.com A` → `172.67.218.62`, `104.21.83.86` (Cloudflare). EXECUTED `dig +short app.libriant.com A` → empty. EXECUTED `dig +short www.libriant.com A` → empty. EXECUTED `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 8 https://admin.libriant.com/` → `curl: (28) Operation timed out`. READ cutover-three-hosts.md:82-88 — the measured DNS block lists only libriant.com, app.libriant.com and the dead box; admin.libriant.com is absent.
fix: Add the real, current DNS inventory to cutover-three-hosts.md Step 1 (it should be re-derived with dig at cutover time, not quoted from August). Repoint admin.libriant.com to 195.201.13.95 in the same change as the app record, and confirm Cloudflare SSL/TLS mode is Full (strict) before either goes live — that setting is the only thing standing between a stale record and a reassigned IP.
verification: DNS RE-MEASURED TODAY: `dig +short admin.libriant.com A` → 172.67.218.62, 104.21.83.86 (Cloudflare, proxied); `dig +short app.libriant.com A` → empty; `dig +short www.libriant.com A` → empty. READ cutover-three-hosts.md:57-68 — the Step 1 measured-DNS block lists libriant.com, app.libriant.com and 178.104.32.176 only; admin.libriant.com is genuinely absent, and no later step repoints or deletes it. That much is true. THE SECURITY IMPACT DOES NOT FOLLOW. The finding's headline harm is 'proxies to a stranger's server ... if Cloudflare's SSL/TLS mode is anything other than Full (strict)'. READ docs/deployment-hetzner.md:448-459: the same repo instructs Full (strict) and lists the record in its DNS table — `| A | admin | 195.201.13.95 | Proxied |`. So (a) the correct target IS documented, just not in the cutover doc, and (b) under the documented mode a stale origin yields a 526, not a transparent proxy to a third party. The origin IP behind the record is also not observable from outside Cloudflare — the finding asserts 178.104.32.176 without evidence. THE 'COMMERCIAL' HARM IS NOT DISTINCTIVE EITHER: I measured `curl --max-time 15 https://admin.libriant.com/` → 000 at 15.00s AND `curl --max-time 15 https://libriant.com/` → 000 at 15.00s. The admin host hangs exactly like the apex, which is documented known state. WHAT SURVIVES, AND IS WORTH FIXING: an operator following cutover-three-hosts.md end to end adds `app`, verifies TLS, and never touches `admin` — so the host that serves the admin panel (where library edit-requests are approved and plans are set) is broken on day one. Loud, not silent; discovered at the first admin login. Medium.

title: The offer terms tell the first five libraries the system 'passed a full security audit', which is not what happened
what: programme-terms.en.md states, as a term of the offer: 'The system **passed a full security audit** before release and is covered by automated tests that run on every change to the code.' The site's own /en/security page contradicts this and is the accurate one: 'It was an internal review, not certification by an independent body, and we do not present it as one.' The only review on record is docs/audit/preprod-final-2026-06-21, a self-audit which certified this codebase as ready while the disaster-recovery restore path had never once worked — a defect found two months later on 2026-08-22 and fixed only then. This audit, run today, is producing further blockers.
impact: The offer terms are the document a school bursar or a municipal committee files. 'Passed a full security audit' reads to that reader as an external assessment. It is a claim that cannot be substantiated if asked for the report, and the honest version already exists 300 metres away on the same site — which makes the discrepancy look like the terms were written to close rather than to inform. The site's whole positioning rests on 'we tell you what we do not have'; this is the one sentence that breaks it.
evidence: READ programme-terms.en.md, section 'Security and availability', first bullet. READ pages.en.json /en/security, section 'A security review before release': 'The system went through a systematic security and reliability review... It was an internal review, not certification by an independent body, and we do not present it as one.' The brief for this audit states docs/audit/preprod-final-2026-06-21 'certified this codebase as ready. The DR restore was broken the entire time and had never once worked.'
fix: Rewrite the bullet to match /en/security — 'went through an internal security and reliability review before release; not an independent certification' — and add the automated-test sentence separately, which is true (verify.yml runs unit + integration + dr:drill on every push). Changing marketing copy is a commit and a full deploy (docs/cutover-three-hosts.md, 'What changed operationally'), so make this edit before the site is first published, not after.
verification: BOTH TEXTS READ AND THE CONTRADICTION IS REAL. `grep -rn -i 'security audit|passed a full' apps/site/content/` → programme-terms.en.md:64 'The system **passed a full security audit** before release'. pages.en.json /en/security reads 'The system went through a systematic security and reliability review before it was offered to a library... It was an internal review, not certification by an independent body, and we do not present it as one.' Two documents on one domain, one of which is a term of the offer, saying different things about the same event. Confirmed. SEVERITY INFLATED. No user suffers, no system misbehaves, nothing breaks at 3am; the harm is reputational and commercial and it is speculative ('costs the deal'). It is also a one-line copy edit that must simply be made before the site is first published. That is a medium, not a high — at high it competes with backups that do not exist and mail that does not send. Downgraded on severity only; the substance is correct and the fix should be taken.

title: 'Five places, given in order of application' is a hand-maintained JSON literal that requires a full CI run and a manual deploy to change, and is wired to nothing
what: `offer.spotsRemaining` is a constant in site.config.json. It gates the public form server-side (applications.controller.ts:51: `if (config.offer.spotsRemaining <= 0) redirect`) and is rendered as a scarcity counter on the home page (apps/site/src/pages.ts:246). Nothing decrements it: it is not derived from the `applications` table, not from the count of provisioned tenants, and not from any admin action. Changing it is a commit, a full verify run and a manual on-box deploy — docs/cutover-three-hosts.md says so explicitly ('`offer.spotsRemaining` is a commit too... It is now a full CI run'). Separately, tenant signup at app.libriant.com/signup is fully self-serve with no closed-registration switch anywhere in the platform settings, so the pool of libraries in the system is unrelated to the pool of applications.
impact: The number on the home page is a claim made to every visitor and will be wrong within days of the campaign — either stale-high (advertising places already promised, so the sixth applicant is told no after being told five remained) or stale-low. Because closing the offer is also a deploy, the form cannot be shut quickly: if all five go in one morning, the sixth through twentieth applications are accepted by a form that should have closed.
evidence: READ site.config.json:16 `"spotsRemaining": 5`. READ applications.controller.ts:48-53 — the gate reads the compiled constant. EXECUTED `grep -rn spotsRemaining apps/ scripts/` — five call sites, all reads; no writer. EXECUTED `grep -rn 'signupsEnabled|SIGNUP_ENABLED|signup_enabled' apps/api/src` → no matches; there is no way to close registration.
fix: Move the counter behind the platform-settings table (the same mechanism as billing.enabled, which already has an admin UI and cache invalidation) so closing the offer is a click, and have the marketing page read it at request time via the /apply host rather than baking it into a static build. Failing that, decide before launch who checks the applications table daily and how fast a deploy can close the form, and write that number down.
verification: RE-VERIFIED WITH MY OWN GREP. `grep -rn spotsRemaining apps/ scripts/` → five sites: site.config.json:16 (`"spotsRemaining": 5`), apps/site/src/pages.ts:190 and :246 (the public scarcity counter), apps/site/src/shell.ts:30 (the type), and apps/api/src/applications/applications.controller.ts:51 (`if (config.offer.spotsRemaining <= 0) redirect`). Every one is a read; there is no writer anywhere. READ applications.controller.ts:5 — `import siteConfigRaw from '@libriant/site/site.config.json' with { type: 'json' }`, i.e. the API's gate is a compiled-in constant, so changing it requires a code change and a redeploy of the API, not just a site rebuild. THE SECOND CLAIM ALSO HOLDS: `grep -rn 'signupsEnabled|SIGNUPS_ENABLED|SIGNUP_ENABLED|signup_enabled|registrationOpen' apps/api/src packages/` → no matches, and platform-settings.service.ts carries exactly one key (BILLING_ENABLED_KEY, lines 37/48/90) — so there is no admin switch that closes registration or the offer. Confirmed at medium: the number on the home page is a claim to every visitor that nothing keeps true, and closing the form is a full CI run plus a manual on-box deploy.

title: There is no customer-facing incident procedure: the handbook's 'When it breaks' never says tell the libraries, and the DPA commits to breach notification with no path to deliver it
what: Part 9 is a competent infrastructure runbook — symptom-indexed, honest about ordering, correct about not rebooting a degraded array. It is silent on every customer-facing action. It never mentions the product's own incident tooling: MAINTENANCE_HARD (documented only in deployment-hetzner.md:762), the `system-mode` states (maintenance / read_only / out_of_order / under_construction, schema.prisma:159-165) or the announcements feature that pushes a banner to tenants. It contains no template for what to say, no decision on when to say it, and no list of who to say it to. Meanwhile locales/en/legal/dpa.md:110-114 commits: 'We will notify you **without undue delay** after becoming aware of a personal-data breach affecting Controller Personal Data' — a GDPR Art. 33(2) processor obligation whose only delivery channel is email, which does not work (finding 01), to a contact list that exists only as rows in the tenants table.
impact: The first customer-visible incident will be improvised by one person at an inconvenient hour, deciding in the moment whether to flip maintenance mode, whether to post an announcement, and how to reach five libraries. For a personal-data breach that improvisation is a compliance failure with a clock on it: 'without undue delay' is measured from awareness, and the notification path has to be established before it is needed, not during.
evidence: READ server-handbook.md Part 9 in full — 9.1 through 9.9 cover down/disk/OOM/CPU/RAID/postgres/TLS/firewall/bad-deploy; `grep -n 'announcement|system-mode|MAINTENANCE_HARD|status page' docs/server-handbook.md` returns nothing. READ dpa.md:110-114. READ schema.prisma:159-165 for the SystemModeKind enum the runbook does not mention.
fix: Add a Part 9.0 to the handbook: the three customer-facing levers in order of severity (announcement banner → system-mode read_only/maintenance → MAINTENANCE_HARD at the edge), who to tell and on what channel, and a two-paragraph holding statement to fill in. Add a separate short breach-notification checklist keyed to the DPA's own wording, including where the five libraries' contact addresses live and a channel that does not depend on the app being up.
verification: THE FALSIFIABLE HALF IS DECISIVE AND I RE-RAN IT. `grep -n -i 'announcement|system-mode|system mode|MAINTENANCE_HARD|status page|read_only' docs/server-handbook.md` returns NOTHING — not one hit in the whole handbook. The Part 9 headings are 9.1 Something is down / 9.1.1 The app is down / 9.2 Disk full / 9.3 Out of memory / 9.4 High CPU / 9.5 RAID degraded / 9.6 Postgres will not start / 9.7 TLS / 9.8 Locked out by the firewall / 9.9 A deploy broke production — infrastructure only, no customer-facing step anywhere. Meanwhile the product ships the levers: schema.prisma:159-165 defines SystemModeKind {normal, maintenance, read_only, out_of_order, under_construction} and there is an announcements feature and an admin page for each. That is the finding: incident tooling was built and the incident runbook does not know it exists. THE DPA COMMITMENT IS REAL: READ locales/en/legal/dpa.md:110-114 — 'We will notify you **without undue delay** after becoming aware of a personal-data breach...' with no notification channel established and, per finding 01, email that does not send. Medium is right: not a Monday outage, but a procedure that has to exist before it is needed rather than during.

title: The single admin account has TOTP mandatory in production, no recovery codes, and no second admin — losing the phone locks the operator out of the admin panel entirely
what: `adminMfaRequired` defaults to `!isDev` (env.ts:311), so in production the bootstrapped admin is forced into MFA enrollment before anything else (admin-auth.guard.ts:65). Enrollment works — /admin/mfa/setup and /verify exist (apps/api/src/support/mfa.controller.ts:26-29) with a UI at apps/web/app/[locale]/admin/(authed)/mfa. But the AdminUser model has no recovery-code field (schema.prisma:805-835: passwordHash, mfaSecretCipher, mfaNonce, mfaKeyId, mfaEnabled — nothing else), `/admin/mfa/disable` is itself behind an authenticated admin session, and the TOTP secret is encrypted under MFA_MASTER_KEY, which ensure-env.sh mints per host and which lives only in the password manager (backups exclude .env.prod by design). scripts/bootstrap-admin.ts is the only way to create an admin and it is a shell command on the box; it does not enroll MFA.
impact: A lost or wiped phone locks the sole operator out of admin.libriant.com — which is where library edit-requests are approved, plans are set, billing is flipped, support access is granted and the applications CSV is served. Recovery is SSH plus a hand-written UPDATE against admin_users. If MFA_MASTER_KEY is lost as well (it is in exactly one place, and by design not in any backup), every enrolled secret becomes undecryptable. This is the same single-point-of-failure shape the handbook already warns about for SSH keys ('keep at least two keys authorized') and does not apply to the admin login.
evidence: READ env.ts:311 `adminMfaRequired: bool('ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED', !isDev)`. READ admin-auth.guard.ts:65 — 403 `mfa_enrollment_required` for any non-/mfa/ non-/auth/ path. EXECUTED `grep -rn 'recovery|backupCode|recoveryCode' apps/api/src/support/mfa.service.ts apps/api/src/support/mfa.controller.ts packages/db-control/prisma/schema.prisma` → one unrelated comment, no field, no endpoint. READ schema.prisma:805-835 for the full AdminUser model. READ ensure-env.sh — `ensure_rand MFA_MASTER_KEY 32`.
fix: Before the box goes into DNS: bootstrap a second owner admin on a separate device and enroll it, and store both TOTP seeds in the password manager alongside MFA_MASTER_KEY. Add the recovery procedure (the exact SQL, and the fact that MFA_MASTER_KEY is required to decrypt an existing secret) to server-handbook.md Part 10 as a numbered procedure — it belongs next to 10.3 Rotate a secret.
verification: EVERY LINK IN THE CHAIN CHECKED, AND I WENT LOOKING FOR THE GUARD THAT WOULD KILL IT. READ env.ts:311 `adminMfaRequired: bool('ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED', !isDev)`. READ admin-auth.guard.ts:65-71 — 403 `mfa_enrollment_required` for any path that is not /mfa/ or /auth/. THE OBVIOUS REFUTATION WOULD BE THAT MFA ONLY GATES SUPPORT-KEY REDEMPTION (schema.prisma:815 says so in a comment) AND NOT LOGIN. IT DOES NOT HOLD: READ admin-auth.controller.ts:47-110 — when `mfaEnabled`, the password alone returns 401 `mfa_required` and a wrong code returns 401 `mfa_invalid` after `recordFailure()`. Login genuinely requires the phone. THE SECOND OBVIOUS REFUTATION — 'just re-run scripts/bootstrap-admin.ts' — ALSO FAILS: READ bootstrap-admin.ts:55-85. The existing-admin branch updates fullName, role, passwordHash, failedAttempts, lockedUntil, status, disabledAt. It does NOT touch mfaEnabled or the secret. Only the create branch sets `mfaEnabled: false`. So a lost phone really does require a hand-written UPDATE against admin_users. NO RECOVERY CODES: `grep -rn 'recovery|backupCode|recoveryCode' apps/api/src/support/mfa.service.ts apps/api/src/support/mfa.controller.ts packages/db-control/prisma/schema.prisma` → one unrelated comment (schema.prisma:793, about a BullMQ cold-start index). READ the full AdminUser model, schema.prisma:805-836: passwordHash, mfaSecretCipher, mfaNonce, mfaKeyId, mfaEnabled, and no recovery field. Confirmed at medium.

title: In-app help is four articles and is installed by a best-effort step that cannot fail a deploy — yet the site sells it as one of only four support mechanisms
what: prod-bootstrap.sh runs `pnpm ingest:help || echo '[bootstrap] help ingest skipped (non-fatal)'` — a failure is swallowed and the deploy goes green with an empty help centre. The corpus itself is four articles per language: getting-started, adding-members, lending-books, reservations. There is nothing on returning a copy, fines, importing a file, exporting data, custom fields, staff and roles, barcode scanning, the desktop app, or settings — including no article on the data export, which is the single feature the site leans on hardest.
impact: apps/site/content/pages.en.json (/en/about) lists exactly four things that stand in for a support organisation: 'two email addresses, step-by-step help inside the application, a reply to every message within two working days, and availability and support terms agreed with you in writing.' One of those four is four articles, and it can silently be zero. Every gap in it converts into an email to the one person who also writes the code — the load the help centre exists to absorb.
evidence: READ prod-bootstrap.sh:46-47. EXECUTED against the live audit environment: `psql -c 'select count(*) from help_articles'` → 0 after migrate+seed, i.e. seeding alone does not populate it; then `pnpm ingest:help` → `[help:en] upserted=4 archived=0 / [help:el] upserted=4 archived=0`; then `select locale, slug, title from help_articles` → 8 rows, the four topics above in each language. EXECUTED `ls locales/en/help/` → 01-getting-started.md, 02-adding-members.md, 03-lending-books.md, 04-reservations.md.
fix: Write the missing everyday articles before the first library is onboarded — returns, fines, import, export, staff and roles at minimum; export first, since it backs the strongest claim on the site. Make the ingest step fatal in prod-bootstrap.sh, or add a readiness check that refuses the deploy when help_articles is empty: an empty help centre is indistinguishable from a working one until a librarian goes looking.
verification: RE-VERIFIED. READ scripts/prod-bootstrap.sh:40-50: the seed step is fatal (`if ! pnpm db:seed; then echo FATAL; exit 1; fi`) but the very next line is `pnpm ingest:help || echo '[bootstrap] help ingest skipped (non-fatal)'` — a failure is swallowed and the deploy goes green. `ls locales/en/help/ locales/el/help/` → exactly four files each: 01-getting-started.md, 02-adding-members.md, 03-lending-books.md, 04-reservations.md. Nothing on returns, fines, import, export, staff and roles, barcode scanning, the desktop app or settings. THE SITE CLAIM IS AS QUOTED: pages.en.json (/en/about) — 'we do not sell tiers of support: no plan buys a faster answer. What does exist is two email addresses, step-by-step help inside the application, a reply to every message within two working days, and availability and support terms agreed with you in writing.' One of the four named support mechanisms is four articles behind a step that cannot fail a deploy. The stated harm — every gap converts into an email to the one person who also writes the code — follows directly and is not speculative at five libraries. Medium stands.

title: Every book create counts the whole catalogue while holding a per-tenant advisory lock
what: `BooksService.create` opens a transaction, calls `quota.enforceWithinTx` which takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock('quota:<tenant>:max_books:')` (apps/api/src/customization/quota.service.ts:63) and then runs `tx.book.count({ where: { archivedAt: null } })`. There is no index that can answer that count, so it is a full scan of `books`. The lock key is per-tenant, so all concurrent book creates for that library serialize behind it. `update` does the same on un-archive (books.service.ts:360). Members have the identical shape (members.service.ts:233, 366).
impact: At 400,000 titles a single book create takes >113 ms of pure counting and 78 MB of buffer traffic, and the advisory lock caps the tenant at roughly 8 book creates per second no matter how many librarians are working. During a cataloguing session with barcode scanning the whole library's write path stalls, and the count evicts the shared buffer cache for every other tenant on the box. It also puts the create within reach of Prisma's 5 s interactive-transaction timeout once the table is cold.
evidence: RAN `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT count(*) FROM books WHERE "archivedAt" IS NULL` on the 400k-book DB: `Parallel Seq Scan on books (rows=130667 loops=3)`, `Buffers: shared hit=955 read=9028`, `Execution Time: 113.207 ms`. Members equivalent: `Seq Scan on members`, 2631 buffers, 14.056 ms. Read: the count runs strictly after the advisory lock (quota.service.ts:63-65) and inside the same transaction as the insert.
fix: Keep a maintained counter instead of counting: a `resource_counters(feature, count)` row in the tenant DB (or `tenants.bookCount` in the control plane) updated in the same transaction as the insert/archive, with the advisory lock guarding the counter row rather than a scan. Failing that, add `CREATE INDEX books_active ON books (id) WHERE "archivedAt" IS NULL` so the count becomes an index-only scan, and shorten the lock window by counting before acquiring it and re-checking cheaply inside.
verification: Code CONFIRMED: quota.service.ts:63-65 takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock` and only then calls `input.count()`, and books.service.ts:203-207 passes `tx.book.count({where:{archivedAt:null}})` inside the same interactive transaction as the insert. Found an AGGRAVATOR the finding missed: the route also runs QuotaInterceptor (apps/api/src/plans/quota.interceptor.ts:19,33 -> countUsage/QUOTA_COUNTERS), so a book create pays the full count TWICE. But two of the finding's numbers do not survive: warm, `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE,BUFFERS) SELECT count(*) FROM books WHERE "archivedAt" IS NULL` is `Parallel Seq Scan`, 9,983 buffers, `Execution Time: 31.594 ms` (the quoted 113 ms was a cold-cache figure), so the advisory lock caps the tenant near 30 creates/sec, not 8; and 30-60 ms is nowhere near Prisma's 5 s interactive-transaction timeout, so 'puts the create within reach of' that timeout is not supported. The members count is 9.8 ms. No bulk path uses this — import-engine.ts tracks quota with an in-memory `quotaUsed` counter. Remaining real harm: ~156 MB of buffer traffic per interactive book create at plan-max size, evicting a 128 MB shared_buffers pool shared by every tenant. Medium.

title: Six append-only tables have no retention sweep at all; the promised audit-retention job does not exist
what: The tenant schema states audit retention is 'governed by the tenant's plan (`audit_log_retention_days` feature) and enforced by a background job'. No such job exists: `apps/api/src/jobs/registry.ts` lists nine jobs and none of them prunes anything, and a repo-wide grep for 'retention' finds only the plan-feature definition (packages/shared/src/features.ts:113), the seed values (7 / 90 / 365 / 1095 / 3650 / 1e9 days) and a comment in apps/site/src/plans.ts:232 admitting 'nothing prunes audit rows'. The same is true of control-plane `email_outbox` (which stores the full `bodyMarkdown` of every message), `audit_log`, `announcement_deliveries`, `stripe_webhook_events` and `support_redemption_attempts` — the only deleteMany calls in the codebase are `bookAuthor` link replacement and `importRowIssue` cleanup.
impact: Tenant DBs grow without bound on a single shared volume, and the largest table is the one with the least value. Concretely: audit_log is what OOM-kills the exporter (performance-01), and it is 609 MB with 3M rows. email_outbox is worse per unit time — with overdue reminders on, the hourly sweep enqueues one row per overdue loan per day (15,000/day measured), each carrying a full message body, into the *shared* control database. Customers were sold a retention figure (7 days on the entry plan) that the product does not honour, so the plan feature is also a false claim.
